title: iOS 27.3 adds new features in six iPhone apps, details here
snippet: iOS 27.3 is coming soon, and it’s a big update for new iPhone features, including additions that span six built-in Apple apps. Here’s what’s new. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.3 is coming soon, and it’s a big update for new iPhone features, including additions that span six built-in Apple apps. Here’s what’s new.

Apple Music

Apple Music adds a pair of upgrades in iOS 27.3. Selfie Sing is an all-new feature that lets you record short videos of yourself singing along to your favorite songs, aided by onscreen lyrics. It’s perfect for sharing on TikTok or other social platforms.

If you’re not the type to share karaoke videos online, another nice iOS 27.3 change is that the lyrics view for songs has gotten an iPhone Duo-inspired upgrade in landscape mode. Now, artwork for the song you’re listening to blends beautifully into the stream of lyrics.

Read more: iOS 27.3 upgrades Apple Music in two ways, here’s what’s new

Safari

Safari is getting several exciting new features in iOS 27.3, including:

Vertical Tabs

Adaptive Dark Mode

Siri AI can now perform many new Safari actions, and on-screen awareness supports full webpages, not just what’s in view

These updates are joined by a new Global Privacy Control setting that’s intended to ultimately prevent cookie consent popups.

Read more: iOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 add Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and more to Safari

Health

Apple’s Health app gets a major overhaul in iOS 27.3, though only for Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhones.

The new Health app has an Insights tab for personalized data visualization and guidance, Longevity tab for tracking your health age, and there are new features like educational videos, movement evaluations, and the ability to order labs that get automatically imported into the app.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds all-new Apple Health app, details here

Apple TV

The Apple TV app is gaining two new types of videos in iOS 27.3 that don’t require an Apple TV subscription (though currently it’s only $6.99/month to subscribe, over 50% off).

Vertical video is coming with a new Clips feature that lets you browse short samples of Apple TV shows and movies in a TikTok-style vertically scrolling format.

Video podcasts are also coming to the TV app, with the option to automatically sync playback from Apple Podcasts inside the TV app.

Read more: iOS 27.3 brings vertical video and video podcasts to Apple TV app

Fitness

Apple Fitness+ is getting a big expansion in iOS 27.3 with a new Gym Strength program.

Gym Strength lets you build a strength program that fits your schedule and the equipment you have on hand. It’s fully customizable and provides Apple’s best offering yet for traditional strength training. 

Whether you’re brand new to strength training or just benefit from some additional structure, Gym Strength is a great reason to try out Fitness+.

Read more: Apple announces Fitness+ Gym Strength program with personalized workout plans

Freeform

Apple’s Freeform app gets a handful of improvements in iOS 27.3, including new text styling options and preset background colors to choose from. You can also generate custom shapes using Apple Intelligence.

If you’re using Freeform on iPad and subscribe to Apple Creator Studio, you’ll also be able to open images directly in Pixelmator Pro to make edits there, and those edits will automatically update on your Freeform board.

Which new iOS 27.3 features are you most excited about? Let us know in the comments.

AirPods 5

AirPods 5 were introduced in September and come in two different versions. Unlike their predecessors, both versions of AirPods 5 offer Active Noise Cancellation. They differ in the charging case, battery life, and volume control. The base model AirPods 5 ($129) come with a case that can only charge via USB-C.

The case for the higher-end AirPods 5 ($149) supports wireless charging and Find My. You also get one extra hour of battery life. The higher-end model also adds on-stem volume control, so you can adjust the volume just by swiping up or down on one of the earbud stems.

AirPods Pro 3

AirPods Pro 3 are Apple’s most capable earbuds, even with the introduction of AirPods 5 this year. They offer an in-ear fit and come with five foam-infused silicone ear tip sizes. title: HomeKit Weekly: Lafaer’s 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes an annoying automation in Apple Home
snippet: Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar. more…
fullText:
Motion-based automations are generally straightforward in Apple Home. The only carve-out is lighting, because some rooms are hard to judge by time of day alone. Depending on the windows and placement against the sun, some rooms might need light-based automations earlier in the day than others. The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor fixes that with a light sensor most motion sensors lack, along with mmWave radar.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

A standard motion sensor uses PIR, which only detects movement, and that works fine in many situations. If you’re still for long periods, you’re invisible, and the automation assumes the room is empty. The Lafaer LWR02 pairs PIR with 2.4 GHz mmWave radar. The PIR-based motion sees you walking in, and the radar sees the minor stuff, like breathing and shifting on the couch, so the room stays “occupied” for as long as you are in it. The two together also reduce false positives from ceiling fans, curtains, and the dog, because the radar and PIR both must agree before the sensor reports motion.

In Apple Home, that shows up as an occupancy sensor and a motion sensor from the same device.

The light sensor is the key part

“Turn on the lights when someone enters” is a common automation I use, but it can be tricky. What if you only want it when it’s not light outside? Doing it based on time of day sometimes works, but what about depending on where the windows are facing, etc.? You might have a room that gets darker an hour earlier than another room. “Turn on the lights when someone enters, and it’s dark in the room” is what the light sensor can handle for you.

In the Home app, that means triggering a sensor for occupancy, then converting the automation into a Shortcut and adding a condition for the light level. It’s a few extra steps, but it does really give you more fine control over how it works.

Five Apple Home sensors built-in

Presence, motion, light, temperature, and humidity all come from the same device, and each one appears in Apple Home as its own sensor, so you can build automations around whichever ones fit the room.

It’s IPX3-rated, so bathrooms, kitchens, and laundry rooms are fine to use in. Coverage is about 13 feet for presence and 26 for motion across about 120 degrees, which works in a bedroom, office, or bathroom. It’s not going to cover a great room from one corner. The base is a magnetic half sphere, so you can aim it, and it mounts with adhesive or sits on a shelf. I generally like to use the shelf for these types of sensors.

Thread and two AAA batteries

The Lafaer LWR02 is Matter over Thread, so it pairs directly with a HomePod, HomePod mini, or Apple TV 4K with no Lafaer hub or account needed. It runs on two included AAA batteries, is rated for up to two years, and rechargeable AAAs work with it as well. Thread is why a sensor doing this much can last that long on batteries. All sensor data is processed locally, so it only uses a trickle on the batteries.

Wrap up on Lafaer LWR02

Lights that turn off while you’re sitting still in the room are the reason a lot of people stop using motion automations in smart homes. The Lafaer LWR02 fixes that with mmWave radar and then lets you have more granular control of light-based automations based on what’s actually in the environment in the room, not just the time of day.

The Lafaer 5-in-1 presence sensor is available on Amazon.

title: Motorola confirms list of devices getting Android 17 updates
snippet: Motorola has posted an updated list of devices getting its Android 17 update, with a few updates already available and many more left to go. more…
fullText:
Motorola has posted an updated list of devices getting its Android 17 update, with a few updates already available and many more left to go.

With the update now rolling out to select devices, most recently the Razr Fold, Motorola is confirming an official list of devices getting Android 17. 

The list was posted by Motorola Brazil, so this includes devices Motorola doesn’t sell in US markets, and also lists Razr devices without their year naming scheme, rather their international branding – i.e. “Razr (2026)” is “Razr 70.”

As per usual, Motorola’s update rollouts may see timing vary by region. The Razr Fold update, for example, is currently rolling out in some international markets but has yet to land in the US.

Motorola explains what’s new in Android 17 as follows:

New look and customization

Among the new features of Android 17 are improvements to the system interface, with more customization options, new icons, and changes to the layout of buttons and widgets. The Settings menu has been redesigned to make navigation more intuitive and facilitate access to the smartphone’s main functions.

Artificial intelligence in everyday life

With the update, Circle to Search now offers real-time translations, allowing you to understand content in other languages ​​more easily, without having to interrupt your current activity on your smartphone.

Simplified connectivity and sharing

Android 17 enhances connectivity with Instant Hotspot , which simplifies sharing your internet connection between compatible devices. Quick Share has also received improvements to facilitate file transfer, including compatibility with iOS smartphones via QR Code.

Additional security features

Security remains a top priority for the system. The Authentication Failure Lock , a security feature in case of theft, locks the screen after unsuccessful authentication attempts. Meanwhile, Message-Based Fraud Detection enhances the identification of potential threats and fraud. Furthermore, access to emergency calls has become easier and faster.

More control over the visual experience.

The update also improves HDR brightness control, which adjusts the screen intensity to highlight bright details in compatible photos and videos. Users can adjust this brightness for more comfortable viewing, or even disable the feature.

The Motorola Signature 27, the company’s new flagship, ships with Android 17 out of the box.

title: MagSafe Monday: Anker’s MagGo Pro 2 has a built-in fan to keep 25W Qi2.2 charging from slowing down
snippet: The biggest issue with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat. It doesn’t matter if the battery specs say it can charge at Qi2.2 speeds if the heat slows it down after 15 minutes. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro directly targets heat with a built-in fan in the MagSafe battery. more…
fullText:
The biggest issue with Qi 2.2 on MagSafe batteries is the slowdown caused by heat. It doesn’t matter if the battery specs say it can charge at Qi2.2 speeds if the heat slows it down after 15 minutes. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro directly targets heat with a built-in fan in the MagSafe battery.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers looks at the latest and greatest in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry to help you get the most out of your Apple devices that support wireless charging.

Heat is the enemy of MagSafe charging, which is why it slows to a crawl on a hot day and why most MagSafe batteries can’t hold their top speed for an entire charge. Anker’s answer in the MagGo 2 Pro is a small fan inside of it. Anker says it keeps the charging surface below 96.8°F, and the fan adjusts its speed based on what’s plugged in and how the charge is progressing. You can switch between Cool and Silent modes if you don’t want to hear it running at all.

The result of having this fan is a Qi2.2 power bank that actually reaches Qi2.2 speeds for a full charge. Anker rates it at 25% on an iPhone 17 Pro in 10 minutes, then to 50% in 25 minutes, which is the kind of speed you’d normally expect from a wired charging session.

Anker MagGo 2 Pro capacity and recharging

The MagGo 2 Pro battery is 10,000mAh, which is enough for a little over one full charge of an iPhone Pro Max and closer to two on a standard iPhone. Size-wise, it has about the same footprint as the iPhone itself and is roughly an ounce lighter than Anker’s standard MagGo. It’s not a slim battery, but for one with a fan, it’s workable in your travel bag, crossbody, etc.

The single USB-C port works both directions at up to 45 watts. If you plug in a 45-watt charger to it, the MagGo 2 Pro can charge from empty to 80% in under an hour. The same port will charge a Mac or an iPad up to 45 watts in a pinch, which is a nice add-on for a MagSafe battery. You are not going to charge up your MacBook Pro from zero to full with it, but it’s a nice way to get a little charge in an emergency at the airport, etc.

One thing to know before you buy: the cable in the box is a 1-foot USB-C-to-USB-C cable, and Anker says that reaching the full 45-watt recharge speed requires a 45-watt-rated cable. So keep that in mind as you pack for a trip.

Display and stand

Anker put a small display on the side that cycles through six screens with a side button: charging wattage, battery percentage, battery health, and temperature. It’s a nice touch to know you are reaching the 25-watt Qi 2.2 speed.

There’s also a built-in stand that adjusts from flat to 80 degrees and folds back into the body when you’re done. You can also quickly turn off charging if you simply want to use it as a stand. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro comes in Phantom Gray, Burgundy Red, Polar Night Blue, and Starlight Silver.

Wrap up on Anker MagGo 2 Pro

Qi2.2 is the Holy Grail of MagSafe chargers, but as I said in the beginning, it’s irrelevant if the heat throttles it. To get full 25-watt MagSafe charging on the go, you’ll likely need something with a fan, unless you’re in colder weather. The Anker MagGo 2 Pro solves that problem with a built-in fan, a handy side display, and a stand.

The Anker MagGo 2 Pro is available on Amazon and directly from Anker.

title: Apple releases iOS 27.3 public beta 2, new developer beta 2 build
snippet: Apple has released iOS 27.3 public beta 2 for iPhone. Today’s release also includes a new build for iOS 27.3 beta 2 for developers. The update brings new Calendar controls, more Siri AI capabilities, and new features for iPhone Duo. It also includes the redesigned Health app and other changes introduced earlier this month. more…
fullText:
Apple has released iOS 27.3 public beta 2 for iPhone. Today’s release also includes a new build for iOS 27.3 beta 2 for developers. The update brings new Calendar controls, more Siri AI capabilities, and new features for iPhone Duo. It also includes the redesigned Health app and other changes introduced earlier this month.

What’s new in iOS 27.3 public beta 2

The update follows yesterday’s second developer beta and the first public beta on November 5.

Here are the latest changes to try:

iPhone Duo: Unlock with Front Camera lets you unlock the phone using the outer display’s selfie camera. It works only when folded, and payments, passwords, and app authentication still require Touch ID or your passcode. You’ll also need Touch ID or your passcode again after 45 minutes without unlocking. There’s a separate new option to lock the phone when you close it.

Attention Aware: iPhone Duo can keep its outer display awake while you’re looking at it and lower the volume of some alerts. You don’t have to set up face unlock to use these features.

Calendar: Search and new-event controls move to the bottom of the app, making them easier to reach.

Siri AI: You can now ask questions about your Health data, including steps, heart rate, and activity rings. Siri can also use a whole Safari webpage as context, including portions you haven’t scrolled to.

Apple TV: The app adds video podcasts and a feed of vertical clips from Apple Originals.

Apple News+: Puzzles expand to Australia, French Canada, and the UK. The available puzzles differ by region.

Apple has also detailed higher daily usage limits for Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features through eligible iCloud+ plans. Plans with 200GB or more include extra capacity; the 50GB plan keeps standard limits.

See our full iOS 27.3 beta 2 roundup for more on the latest discoveries.

More iOS 27.3 features

The first public beta brought back the redesigned Health app after its earlier preview during iOS 27.2 testing. On iPhones with Apple Intelligence support, Insights collects trends across your health data, while Longevity includes a Health Age comparison based on Apple Watch measurements.

Other changes already available include:

Safari: Vertical Tabs and Adaptive Dark Mode add another tab layout and darken websites without their own dark theme.

Siri AI: More actions across Apple apps include creating playlists, scheduling messages, and adding Journal entries.

iPhone Duo: Reachability moves content left or right for easier one-handed use.

StandBy: More clock customization includes colors, complications, and multiple configurations.

Apple Fitness+: Gym Strength offers a four-week training plan tailored to your goals and equipment.

How to install iOS 27.3 public beta 2

If you’re already testing the public beta, open Settings > General > Software Update to check for the new version.

Joining for the first time? Make a backup, then enroll in the free Apple Beta Software Program using your iPhone’s Apple Account. In Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates, choose iOS 27 Public Beta. Go back to Software Update to download and install it.

What are you trying first in iOS 27.3 public beta 2? Let us know in the comments.

title: ‘The One Ring’ promises to make you the Lord of the Smart Rings
snippet: A special-edition RingConn Gen 3 is The One Ring to rule them all, and you can preorder it now. more…
fullText:
A special-edition RingConn Gen 3 is The One Ring to rule them all, and you can preorder it now.

Lots of people will be picking up smart rings this year as many models go on sale for Black Friday, but one special RingConn smart ring might make you forget about all that. RingConn’s Gen 3 ring has been transformed into The One Ring, which is up for preorder right now for $399 and ships starting December 8.

The limited-edition gold ring features the legendary Black Speech inscription along the outside, which, thankfully, you won’t need to run through a fire to see. title: macOS 27.3 public beta 2 now available, here’s everything new
snippet: After releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the company is now rolling out the public beta for users looking to try the new features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming. more…
fullText:
After releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the company is now rolling out the public beta for users looking to try the new features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming.

Apple releases macOS 27.3 Golden Gate public beta 2

Last Monday, Apple released macOS 27.3 beta 2, with new privacy controls for Full Disk Access and automation tools, and the availability of Apple Intelligence in China.

Those came alongside several new features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

And speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing users to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing new tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful update, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and users on the public beta can now try out these new features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

title: Meta throws out its net-zero goal — its competitors should be furious
snippet: Meta walked back its 2030 net-zero goal in its 2026 sustainability report, a decision that could send ripples throughout the tech industry.
fullText:
Meta’s new sustainability report buries the lead: The company is almost certain to miss its own goal to reach net zero by 2030, and it’s refusing to commit to a new timeline.

“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets — so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” wrote Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net-zero and sustainability at Meta, in the introduction to the company’s 2026 sustainability report.

That’s a lot of words to say that Meta will continue to pollute if that means it can continue its AI rollout.

Such is the risk of voluntary targets. Companies can make and break them with little to lose, betting — often rightly — that they can ignore them with just a small hit to public opinion, which is fickle anyway. (Remember the Cambridge Analytica scandal? Most people don’t.) There’s almost no risk to the bottom line.

“We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline and interim milestone. We’ll continue investing in emissions reductions and reporting our progress annually,” a Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch.

A few years ago, Meta was arguably one of the better corporate stewards of the climate. The company has been one of the largest purchasers of clean power, and it set ambitious goals for water conservation. 

More recently, though, its multibillion-dollar bet on natural gas at its Hyperion data center in Louisiana has undone much of that progress. Natural gas may burn cleaner and more efficiently than coal, but its impact on global warming can be just as bad when the leaky infrastructure needed to burn it is factored in.

Despite years of clean power procurement, Meta’s greenhouse gas emissions have more than doubled in the last four years. Between 2024 and 2025, its data center emissions increased more than 12 times, and Hyperion isn’t online yet.

That commitment to natural gas led to the company’s departure from RE100, a corporate renewable energy initiative, in July. The company had been part of the group for a decade, though the two split after RE100 started requiring more rigorous reporting toward renewable energy targets. 

“When we set our net zero emissions goal, we anticipated steady growth, falling clean energy costs, and changes in the broader system that would enable progress at the pace we envisioned,” they added. “The reality has been far more complex. Demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected, arriving on a timeline measured in quarters rather than decades, and meeting it has meant building at a pace and scale the industry has never attempted.”

That’s all true, but when put that way, it sounds like Meta has little agency in the matter. But the company’s decision to chase AI was a conscious one.

You could argue that Meta has a fiduciary duty to chase after its peers, which have also dived headfirst into AI. But there’s precious little data to support the idea that AI will be a profit driver for a company like Meta, which is almost entirely consumer-focused. 

CEO Mark Zuckerberg is optimistic that improving Muse’s energy efficiency will turn that around, but how much will everyday people be willing to pay for software that translates your offhand thoughts into surreal memes? Or monitors your emails so you won’t forget to reply to your mom? Meta is betting that it’ll be enough to support a $200 billion-plus data center, and probably more.

The choice of the fuel to power those AI ambitions was also a conscious one. Natural gas power plants, besides being able to run 24/7, are actually not a great fit for AI data centers. Turbines like to run at constant speeds, while AI data centers’ energy requirements surge and sag depending on the load. They need batteries as a buffer, which begs the question: Why not just connect to the grid and use batteries to bridge any gaps during times of peak demand? That’s what one expert recommends. 

Meta’s bet on natural gas appears mistimed. Long-duration energy storage is coming into its own — and geothermal energy appears poised to become the next major power source on the grid in the U.S. Companies like Fervo, Mazama, and Quaise have been logging milestones at a rapid clip, potentially unlocking tens of gigawatts of capacity. The technology isn’t competitive with natural gas today, but it very well could be in the mid-2030s, just a few years after Meta completes Hyperion. Geothermal is also not vulnerable to supply chain shocks, like what happened with natural gas and the Iran War.

Beyond that, the company’s decision to abandon its 2030 net-zero goal risks fomenting the sort of backlash that leads to regulations with real teeth. Such regulations won’t just apply to Meta, and the broader industry would be justified in their frustration.

In that light, Meta’s timing couldn’t be worse. Surveys show the general public doesn’t hold AI or data centers in high esteem, rightly sensing that the infrastructure development is driving a rapid and often-unchecked expansion of polluting infrastructure. 

The tech industry has spent over a decade trying to prove that it would be different from previous industrial juggernauts like oil and gas or automobile manufacturing. In a single PDF, Meta might have undone much of that goodwill. After this, who will trust another tech company’s voluntary net-zero goals?

Tim De Chant is a senior climate reporter at TechCrunch. He has written for a wide range of publications, including Wired magazine, the Chicago Tribune, Ars Technica, The Wire China, and NOVA Next, where he was founding editor. 

De Chant is also a lecturer in MIT’s Graduate Program in Science Writing, and he was awarded a Knight Science Journalism Fellowship at MIT in 2018, during which time he studied climate technologies and explored new business models for journalism. title: The Google Home app is better than Nest alone ever was, mostly

fullText:
The Nest app is officially dead, but it’s worth taking a step back and remembering that, while there are some rough edges, the Google Home app is a better smart home experience than Nest alone ever could have been.

9to5Google Weekender by Ben Schoon is a part of our free newsletter that also includes ‘Inbox,’ a twice-weekly roundup of key stories from around the web by Daniel Bader. The Nest app has been on life support for years now. Google has been migrating legacy products into the Home app for a while and the last few puzzle pieces came in Nest Protect support, the death of the earliest Nest Thermostats, and other assorted adjustments. 

	

Google retiring Nest app and Google Assistant on speakers, displays in 2027

Realistically, even long-time Nest users have had no reason to continue using the app over Google Home.

Having been personally, deeply invested in Google’s vision for the smart home over the past decade, I’ll say that the Google Home app we have today is better than the Nest app ever was or ever could be. A huge part of that comes from Google Home’s ability to pull together devices from third-party ecosystems. Being able to control your entire smart home from a single app is how the smart home always should have been, and between Google’s work and the Matter standard, we’re finally able to enjoy that pretty seamlessly for the most part. Automations, Google’s actually-useful AI features, and more only sweeten the deal. I’m also a big fan of what the Home app has become from a UX perspective. While there are always rough edges and bugs to clean up, the customizable homepage and well-organized sections make for a good – not perfect, but good – experience for the end user.

That said, there is one thing that the Nest app’s limited scope benefitted from, and that’s a focus on making your own product great. 

Google’s move to the Home app for Nest devices has been a 5-year run of trying to clean things up, improve on the app, and basically bring back the way things were in the Nest app as far as the first-party cameras and thermostats are concerned. It’s taken ages, but we’re finally up to speed, mostly. I still hate that you have to reset Nest Cams to change Wi-Fi when the Nest app just let you change it, and the Nest app’s settings were much less overwhelming, but I’d say the pros far outweigh the cons at this point.

The Nest app was good at its job, but the Google Home app is a worthy successor, finally, and now the Nest app can finally rest. I mostly think the same applies to Gemini vs Google Assistant, with the newer assistant a better overall experience, but it’s easier to poke holes in that argument.

Disagree? What do you think of the Google Home app, and were you still using the Nest app?

fullText:
Apple has just released its first post-launch software update for the HomeView, version 27.2.1 which includes several bug fixes. Here’s how to install it.

HomeView 27.2.1 is available now to install via Home app with Siri AI bug fixes

Last week the Apple HomeView arrived in users’ homes and immediately required a software update to version 27.2.

But now, Apple has already released its first post-launch update.

HomeView software 27.2.1 is now available for all users.

You can install the update by opening the Home app on your iPhone then tapping the three dots in the top-right corner, opening Home Settings, and going to the ‘Software Update’ section.

Apple has not yet published release notes for the update, so it’s unclear what changes it introduces.

It’s possible HomeView 27.2.1 will address some of the Siri AI issues that users have been encountering and sharing online, or other bugs. It likely also includes security updates that first shipped in iOS 27.2.1 and related builds.

We’ll report back when we have more information.

This update provides important bug fixes for your HomeView, including fixes for the following issues:

Setting up a Shared Album on the Photos face may prevent the device from downloading support for Siri, causing Siri to be unavailable

Pairing with an iPhone or iPad running the iOS or iPadOS 27.3 beta may cause Siri requests to fail

Connecting another home hub device may unexpectedly remove HomeView from your home

title: Pebblebee Alert Dispatch lets an actual human respond to your emergency, triggered by Find Hub trackers
snippet: While many services are turning to AI in place of an actual human being, Pebblebee’s new Alert Dispatch brings the help of a real person into an emergency situation, and it all starts with your Find Hub tracker. more…
fullText:
While many services are turning to AI in place of an actual human being, Pebblebee’s new Alert Dispatch brings the help of a real person into an emergency situation, and it all starts with your Find Hub tracker.

Pebblebee launched its Alert feature in 2025 as a way to use a Clip 5 tracker for Find Hub as a siren in an emergency. The company later added an optional live location-sharing feature to this, and also released “Halo” as an emergency siren first, tracker second with a special design.

Pebblebee ‘Halo’ Android Find Hub tracker doubles as a flashlight and safety siren [Video]

Now, “Alert Dispatch” takes the whole system up a notch.

Instead of relying solely on location sharing and the siren, Pebblebee’s Alert Dispatch assigns an actual human being to the situation, with a trained dispatch agent reaching out first over SMS or a call, then pulling in emergency responders if the situation calls for it. The feature works with Clip 4, Clip 5, and Halo. 

	

Pebblebee explains:

Alert Dispatch connects Pebblebee users with a trained dispatch agent when they trigger an Alert, starting with a text and escalating to an Emergency call if they don’t respond. With an attempt to send help when users cannot confirm they’re safe, plus live location sharing and private Check-In calls on Clip 5 and Halo, it adds another layer of support when calling for help isn’t an option.

Pebblebee Alert Dispatch runs in partnership with Noonlight, with an alert triggered by disconnecting Halo or rapidly pressing the button on Clip trackers. Pricing is as follows:

1 Person: $5.99/month or $49.99/year

4 People: $19.99/month or $159.99/year

8 People: $39.99/month or $319.99/year

Sony’s DualSense Wireless Controller for the PlayStation 5 features immersive haptic feedback and resistance triggers, which feel great to use. It offers a built-in mic, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a mute button; it also works with PC, macOS, and mobile devices via Bluetooth or USB-C.

$299

The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

$18

With 12.4mm drivers, active noise cancellation, and an IP54 rating, the CMF Buds 2A offer high-end features at an affordable price. You can also customize the sound, adjust ANC levels, and find the earbuds using the Nothing X app.

$60

Anker’s durable travel adapter delivers up to 100W of power and works in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does offer a trio of USB-C ports and a nifty LCD display to keep tabs on the charge percentage.

$35

007 First Light, a third-person stealth action game from the studio behind Hitman, is arguably the best action game we’ve played this year. It features a wide variety of missions that have you sneaking through enemy territory, engaging in hand-to-hand combat, and taking part in high-speed car chases — you know, classic Bond stuff. Read our review.

$40

Fanttik’s rechargeable electric screwdriver features three adjustable torque settings, a built-in LED light, and 16 S2 hardened steel bits for tackling everything from furniture assembly to small electronics repairs. It also comes with a magnetic storage case and supports USB-C.

$649

Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

$14

No one should have to deal with a rat’s nest behind their desk when devices like Anker’s 2-in-1 USB-C cable exist. The handy USB-C cable splits at the end, giving you the ability to charge up to two devices from a single port. That means you can split power between a phone and tablet or juice a 16-inch MacBook Pro to 50 percent in just 20 minutes using a single port.

$45

The Nintendo Switch 2 has 256GB of storage, but that won’t get you very far if you’ve built up a medium-sized digital game library. Samsung’s P9 256GB microSD express card doubles the console’s available storage.

$69

You likely won’t find wireless earbuds with a more striking appearance than Nothing’s Ear 3A. They also sound fantastic, boast active noise cancellation, and offer robust EQ settings, making them a great pick for the price. Read our review.

$100

Ember’s latest smart mug is designed to keep your coffee at the ideal temperature for up to three hours, with five temp settings between 120 and 145 degrees Fahrenheit. The third-gen version is similar to prior models; however, you can now adjust the heat settings directly on the mug and throw it in the dishwasher, which wasn’t the case before.

$700

Despite being an entry-level variant of the B6 OLED, this model features four HDMI 2.1 ports, a 120Hz refresh rate, a capable processor, and pixel-perfect image quality and contrast for any content you want to watch. Lower brightness is likely the biggest compromise with getting a cheaper OLED.

$150

JBL’s Tour One M3 noise-canceling headphones come with a touchscreen-equipped wireless transmitter that lets you wirelessly listen to audio from in-flight entertainment systems and other devices without Bluetooth. They also offer solid active noise cancellation and last up to 70 hours on a charge.

$698

Hisense’s 2026 CanvasTV is a 4K QLED TV that doubles as wall art when you’re not watching. It features a matte, anti-glare display and runs on Google’s excellent TV software; it’s also a great pick for gamers thanks to its snappy 144Hz variable refresh rate and a pair of HDMI 2.1 ports.

$369

The Elegoo Centauri Carbon 2 Combo is a beginner-friendly 3D printer that supports four filament spools. It features an enclosed build chamber, automatic bed leveling, and a large touchscreen, making it easy to produce reliable prints.

$48

Moft’s Trackable Tripod Wallet is a MagSafe-compatible wallet that holds two cards and folds into an adjustable phone stand or small tripod. It also supports both Apple’s Find My network and Google’s Find Hub, offers Qi wireless charging, and includes a detachable shutter remote for taking photos.

$54

Govee’s Table Lamp 2 is way more fun than your average table lamp. The color-changing device boasts built-in scheduling and more than 60 dynamic lighting effects, including preset scenes for various holidays. You can even create custom color combos for when “Dandelion” and other presets just aren’t cutting it.

$200

Birdfy’s metal smart bird feeder features a wide-angle 4K camera that lets you get an up-close look at visiting birds, along with a 1.8-liter seed capacity and a built-in solar panel for charging. It also offers free AI-powered recognition of more than 6,000 bird species.

$649

Bambu Lab’s P2S Combo is a 3D printer that can print in multiple colors and automatically dry its materials to help improve print quality. It also features a 5-inch touchscreen, a built-in camera for monitoring prints remotely, and AI-powered tools that can detect printing problems.

$35

Headspace makes it easier to build mindfulness into your everyday life, whether you’re looking to manage stress, improve focus, or get a better night’s sleep. An annual subscription gives you access to hundreds of guided meditations, breathing exercises, and other tools for beginners and experienced users alike.

$1000

The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets, thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

$30

Saros is a third-person sci-fi shooter in which players fight alien enemies on a mysterious planet trapped in a time loop. The PS5 exclusive features fast-paced combat, a variety of powerful weapons, and challenging boss fights. Read our review.

$199

Bose’s second-gen QuietComfort Headphones build on the original with better sound quality and support for lossless audio over USB-C. They also offer improved noise cancellation and are more comfortable thanks to their lack of “eardrum suck.”

$300

Garmin’s midrange Forerunner watch has an OLED display, a week’s worth of battery life, and dual-frequency GPS for better accuracy. Read our review.

$1495

The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost human-like navigation, tackling high-pile rugs, and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review.

$22

Azul is a game in which you arrange patterned tiles in order to create the most beautiful tapestry possible. Arranging tiles in a strategic sequence will help you build your score while limiting your opponents’ ability to grow theirs.

$380

The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

$42

Arguably the best thing to come out of The Book of Boba Fett was the Mandalorian’s N-1 Starfighter, which Lego has recreated here in miniature. It’s not quite as impressive as the 1,802-piece version, but the cheaper set still packs plenty of detail, including a spring-loaded shooter.

$169

Nothing’s first pair of over-ear headphones feature a retro transparent design and high-end features like active noise cancellation, spatial audio with head tracking, and plush ear pads. They also feature a paddle button that allows you to control music playback. Read our review.

$400

Amazon’s 12.3-inch Alexa Tablet 12 Pro runs Android with access to the Google Play Store, unlike the company’s Fire tablets. It also features built-in Alexa Plus integration, a dedicated Kindle reading mode, and up to 16 hours of battery life. Read our hands-on impressions.

$698

Samsung’s last-gen Frame is a 4K QLED TV that displays art on its anti-glare matte screen when not in use. It also supports Dolby Atmos, HDR10 Plus, and popular streaming apps, with refresh rates up to 144Hz on larger models.

$8

TP-Link’s smart smart plug lets you remotely control lamps, fans, and other appliances using your phone or voice commands. It supports Matter, so it works with all major smart home platforms, and lets you set schedules and timers to automatically turn devices on or off.

$99

Google’s latest pair of wireless earbuds feature crisp sound quality, a comfortable design, and solid active noise cancellation, which is great considering the budget-friendly price tag. They even offer built-in support for Gemini and, unlike the entry-level AirPods, a purple option! Read our review.

$700

Roku now makes some of the most affordable, yet feature-packed 4K OLED TVs available for gamers or movie lovers looking for a big TV upgrade under $1,000. The Pro Series LX with better brightness, faster refresh rate, and a polarizer to reduce reflections starts at $200 more.

$280

If you’re on a tight budget, but want spectacular contrast and brightness control that only an OLED can provide, here’s a deal for you. Alienware’s 1440p 27-inch QD-OLED monitor with 240Hz refresh rate is selling at its lowest price yet. Read our hands-on.

$130

Soundcore makes some of the best wireless earbuds you’ve never heard of — and the Liberty 5 Pro may be its best pair yet. The sleek buds deliver powerful noise cancellation, good sound, and surprisingly fabulous call quality for less than Apple’s latest AirPods.

$60

A great first portable music player/speaker for kids. It uses insertable NFC cards (sold separately) to play music and stories to keep kiddos occupied and entertained without zoning out in front of the TV. This model supports Bluetooth and 3.5mm for private listening, too.

$40

The latest entry in the long-running survival horror series returned in 2026, with two different styles of gameplay (tense first-person and guns-blazing third-person perspectives) via its dual protagonists. Read our review.

$180

The latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review.

$150

The big difference between the Superstrike and other gaming mice lies beneath its main two mouse buttons. It uses haptic actuators instead of mechanical switches, allowing for lower latency and more longevity.

$209

The Nex Playground’s motion-controlled gameplay is designed for ages five and up. It comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whack-a-Mole Deluxe, but many more titles are available via a subscription. It’s a ton of fun for kids. This is the lowest price so far in 2026. Read our review.

$55

With a 4.3-inch E Ink screen, the Xteink X4 is smaller and more pocketable than any Kindle and Kobo model currently available. It has some drawbacks — it’s limited to TXT and EPUB files — but it’s great for tinkering; it also has a magnetic mount so you can stick it to the back of MagSafe-ready phones.

$299

The Ring 5 is a fantastic entry point for new users. While short on improvements over its thicker predecessor, it’s hard not to appreciate that it manages to deliver similar battery life despite being thinner. Read our review.

$419

Nothing has changed in terms of aesthetics, but the Max 2 deliver better sound and some new features. Not exactly worth upgrading for, but fantastic for those who are considering them now. Read our full review.

$120

It’s hard to find a cooler lamp than Govee’s Uplighter floor lamp at this price. It can light a room, and display a mesmerizing pattern up your wall and onto your ceiling.

$297

The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.

$55

Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.

$130

Compared to the last-gen base Kindle model (currently $119.99), the Paperwhite is a much better value. It features waterproofing, better battery life, faster page-turning speeds, and a higher pixel density screen that’s slightly larger (7 inches vs. 6 inches)

$239

The water-resistant Sonos Play sits between the Roam 2 and Move 2, offering a balance of portability and room-filling sound. It delivers up to 24 hours of battery life, with a built-in loop for easy carrying. You can also use it as a power bank and pair it with other Sonos speakers over Bluetooth when Wi-Fi isn’t available. Read our review.

$10

LIFX’s dimmable, color-changing bulbs offer Wi-Fi connectivity, simple setup, and Matter compatibility, so they fit seamlessly into any major smart home platform. Best of all, the smart features come at a price that makes buying multipacks more affordable than other brands.

$21

Iniu’s P55-E2 Power Bank is an ultra-slim three-port USB charger that’s capable of fully recharging an iPhone 16 twice. It supports charging speeds of up to 45W via a USB-C port, which can deliver fast recharging for a range of gadgets.

$50

The Echo Dot Max features a flat design and a redesigned sound system, which delivers nearly three times the bass as its predecessor. It also offers improved conversation detection and better noise filtering, thanks to Amazon’s new AZ3 chip. Read our review.

$50

Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Paulene’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.

$40

Whether you primarily drive a car, motorcycle, or a bicycle, the one thing in common with all three modes of transport is the need for a well-inflated tire. This rechargeable 150psi inflator might just save you from a flat (or from being dangerously close to one) when you least expect it.

$749

Google wants to sell you on the Pro’s software features, but it’s the underlying hardware that makes it a stellar Android handset. The build quality is incredible, the larger telephoto sensor is an improvement, and it now supports faster wired speeds and Qi2.2 for up to 25W wireless charging.

$25

In Catan, up to four players strategically compete and trade for resources. The iconic board game ends when one player reaches 10 “victory points,” which is achieved by constructing a sprawling civilization of roads, settlements, and cities using sheep, ore, wheat, and wood.

$115

A 10-inch anti-glare touchscreen that comes in a few design options. It’s a frame that features Alexa, and doubles as a smart speaker. It works with Amazon Photos, which offers unlimited storage for Prime members.

$10

Glocusent’s clip-in reading light features five brightness levels and multiple color temperature settings, ranging from a soft, warm glow that’s great for late-night reading to a brighter light that’s perfect for daytime use. The slim USB light easily slips into your pocket, too, so you can read anywhere, from a cozy bed to a dimly lit train.

$200

This innovative new smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It will also work with the new Aliro standard and be compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking.

$28

Few plants are as festive to have around the house during the holidays as poinsettia. Lego’s 608-piece recreation stands 8 inches tall, includes a “woven-basket” flowerpot, and — unlike the one you undoubtedly received as a gift in the past — requires absolutely no maintenance.

$550

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design.

$26

Twelve South’s entry-level Bluetooth transmitter delivers up to 25 hours of continuous use and lets you connect up to two pairs of headphones to an in-flight entertainment system, making it a great travel companion no matter where you’re going.

$30

The Chamera is not a good camera, but that’s not the point. Kodak’s charming, keychain-friendly tchotchke lets you snap lo-fi memories on a whim, with an ultra-small 1.6-megapixel sensor, a built-in LED flash, and the tiniest amount of storage.

$35

Sucker Punch’s follow-up to Ghost of Tsushima is everything you could want in a sequel. The open-world revenge epic brims with fluid combat and a host of welcome narrative twists, all set against the gorgeous backdrop of Japan’s Edo period. It’s precisely the type of game photo modes were made for, even if you never use them.

$18

The Wuben G5 flashlight is as small as a Zippo lighter, yet far more versatile, with a bright, rotatable light that can shine in numerous colors. It features USB-C charging and has an adjustable clip.

$32

The last-gen JBL Go 4 has been around for a bit, but the pocket-sized Bluetooth speaker still delivers with up to seven hours of runtime, dual-device connectivity, and an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance. You can also pair it with other Go 4 speakers for bigger stereo sound, if desired.

$149

Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 deliver the best noise cancellation and sound quality of any AirPods yet, along with a more comfortable, secure fit and improved water resistance. They also feature built-in heart rate tracking for workouts and support live translations for a handful of languages. Read our review.

title: Deals: Pixel Watch 5 hits Black Friday price at $100 off, Galaxy Watch 9 $110 off, Galaxy Tabs $300 off, more
snippet: Alongside the updated Amazon early Black Friday sale, ongoing all-time low on Google Home Speaker, new all-time lows on the brand new Android Alexa tablets starting from $150, and the $350 price drop on Galaxy Z Fold 8, we have some fresh deals to scope out today as well. Firstly, some Android-ready smartwatches – lucky users can land a solid $110 off Galaxy Watch 9 down at $270 right now and the advertised Black Friday price on the most affordable Pixel Watch 5 is already live at $100 off. We also at least $300 off the current-generation Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 and Samsung’s 2026 4K/5K ViewFinity and M-series monitors at 50% off, but you’ll find a whole lot more below including the lowest price ever on the brand new Fire TV Stick 4K at just $20. more…
fullText:
Alongside the updated Amazon early Black Friday sale, ongoing all-time low on Google Home Speaker, new all-time lows on the brand new Android Alexa tablets starting from $150, and the $350 price drop on Galaxy Z Fold 8, we have some fresh deals to scope out today as well. Firstly, some Android-ready smartwatches – lucky users can land a solid $110 off Galaxy Watch 9 down at $270 right now and the advertised Black Friday price on the most affordable Pixel Watch 5 is already live at $100 off. We also at least $300 off the current-generation Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 and Samsung’s 2026 4K/5K ViewFinity and M-series monitors at 50% off, but you’ll find a whole lot more below including the lowest price ever on the brand new Fire TV Stick 4K at just $20. 

Amazon updates early Black Friday sale with loads of new deals: AirPods, Apple Watch Series 12, Fold 8, PlayStation, more

Best Buy Week 3 Black Friday now live: Apple, 50% off TVs, 40% off kitchen, home theater, more

Most affordable Google Pixel Watch 5 you can buy now live at Black Friday pricing ($100 off)

The official Google Black Friday deals don’t start until tomorrow, but the advertised $100 price drop on Pixel Watch 5 is already live as part of the now updated Amazon early Black Friday sale. If you’re looking to score the most affordable model in the sleek Obsidian black colorway, you can nab one today and get it off your list early. 

Amazon is now offering the 41mm Pixel Watch 5 in Obsidian black down at $299.99 shipped. 

	

This is a regularly $400 Google watch that released this past summer and the most affordable model you can buy at $100 off the list price. It also happens to be sitting at the same price Google told us it will be offering for Black Friday this year right now. 

If there is a different size, color, or config you are after, you’ll need to wait until tomorrow to pull the trigger, but if you do happen to be after the least expensive black model, this is it right now. 

Google officially revealed its upcoming Black Friday deals earlier this month, specifically stating Pixel Watch 5 will be $100 off. That offer will join up to $400 off the Pro Pixel 11 phones, deals on its latest buds, and more. 

It did not mention the 2026 Google Home Speaker or the new Pixel Tag though – arguably two of the best Google gear gifts you buy this year:

Google Home Speaker Jade $80 (Reg. $100)

Google Home Speaker Hazel $80 (Reg. $100)

Current-gen Galaxy Tab S11 now $300 off in early Black Friday sale, up to $505 off open-box

We have already detailed a number of major early Black Friday Samsung deals, from the Fold 8 at $350 off to the Galaxy S26 Ultra at a giant $450 off, but now it’s time for the S11. While the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra has launched, the base S11 remains in the current-generation lineup and now you can score one at $300 off in brand new condition, or up to a giant $505 off in Best Buy open-box condition. 

Amazon is now offering the Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 down at $699.99 shipped for the 128GB, $799.99 for the 256GB, and $999.99 for the 512GB – all three of which are now $300 off the list price in bran new condition and now matched on the official Samsung site. 

Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 128GB $700 (Reg. $1,000)

Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 256GB $800 (Reg. $1,100)

Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 512GB $1,000 (Reg. $1,300)

The S11 remains the current-generation 11-inch flagship Galaxy Tab and the affordable S series Tab in the lineup. Save for a short-lived Prime Day offer at $40 off the list price, this is matching the lowest prices we have tracked on the most affordable model in the last 3 to 4 months. 

For something much lower than though, you’ll want to scope out the Best Buy open-box deals – you’ll find models at up to $505 off the list prices to undercut the early Black Friday deals by a long shot:

Open-box Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 128GB $495 (Reg. $1,000)

Open-box Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 128GB $663 (Reg. $1,000) – excellent condition

Some users are scoring the latest Galaxy Watch 9 as low as $270 right now ($110 off)

The Samsung deals are flying this week with straight up $350 price drops on the popular Galaxy Z Fold 8 and a giant $450 off Galaxy S26 Ultra. While straight up cash deals on the latest Galaxy Watch 9 have been far more rare outside of expensive bundles, the official Samsung site is now serving up a deep $110 discount to bring the price down to $269.99 shipped for some folks. 

Over on the official Samsung site, we are now tracking the 40mm Galaxy Watch 9 down at $269.99 shipped – that’s $110 off the regular $380 list price and one of the best straight up cash deals we have tracked without having to bundle the watch with a more expensive phone. 

There is one caveat here…one big one, the deal doesn’t seem to work for everyone – you might need to try logging in, or adding it to the cart a couple times in order to see the price down this low – try a different browser or private window, or go mobile, or something, or anything. 

If you are one of the lucky ones that can get the price down this low, than you’ll be looking at the lowest price we can find, landing well below the current Amazon list to undercut the best deals we have tracked there since release. 

Scope out more of this week’s best early Black Friday Samsung deals below:

Samsung’s 2026 4K/5K ViewFinity and M-series workstation monitors are nearly 50% off in early Black Friday deals

Amazon’s early Black Friday deals are starting to heat up, and we’re seeing some hefty discounts on Samsung’s ViewFinity and M-series monitors right now. The deals are now live on a bunch of displays, including some of Samsung’s newer 2026 productivity ViewFinity models with sharp 4K and 5K panels, along with its M-series Smart Monitors that bring built-in streaming and other smart features to your desk. These are now down to some of their best prices yet at up to 44% off, making this a great time to upgrade your Mac or Windows workstation ahead of Black Friday. Head below for a closer look at the deals.

Early Black Friday deals on Samsung monitors

Samsung 32-inch ViewFinity S7 (S71H) 4K Monitor $200 (Reg. $290)

And even more…

That’s a whopping $200 discount on its usual $700 price tag, marking a new all-time low for this newer 2026 display. It also earned a spot in our recent Mac display spotlight, and at under $500, it’s a particularly tempting upgrade for a Mac mini or Mac Studio setup. You’re getting a sharp 5120 x 2880 IPS panel with 218 PPI, along with USB-C connectivity, HDMI, DisplayPort, Ethernet, HDR10, and a fully adjustable stand.

All-new Amazon Android Alexa Tablets hit Black Friday all-time lows today from $150 (Up to $130 off)

Amazon’s early Black Friday sale is now offering its new 2026 Fire TV Stick 4K down at $19.99 with free shipping for Prime members or in orders over $35.

Amazon Fire TV Cube, 4K Ultra HD, Wi-Fi 6E: $90 (Reg. $200)

Pick up Anker’s latest HomeKit-ready solar Wall Light Cam S4 or a 2-pack at new lows from $150

Samsung early Black Friday now live: Fold 8/Ultra $350 off, S26 Ultra $450 off, more

Just after the release of the all-new Galaxy SmartTag 3 item trackers from $25 a pop, the early Black Friday Samsung deals are kicking into overdrive this week with Galaxy S26 Ultra at a giant $450 off the list price and Fold 8 at $350 off, however we are also now tracking Gold 8 Ultra at $350 and the Samsung site has started to price match the deep Amazon deals as part of its official Black Friday sale. 

Galaxy Fold 8/Ultra early Black Friday deals:

Galaxy Z Fold 8 256GB $1,550 (Reg. $1,900) – $350 off

Galaxy Z Fold 8 512GB $1,750 (Reg. $2,100) – $350 off

title: iOS 27.3 adds Siri AI usage limits, here’s what counts toward your limit
snippet: Earlier this week, Apple revealed that Siri AI usage limits will be implemented in iOS 27.3 and explained how iCloud+ increases those limits. Now we have a real-world example of what it looks like when limits are hit, and details on what counts toward those limits. more…
fullText:
Earlier this week, Apple revealed that Siri AI usage limits will be implemented in iOS 27.3 and explained how iCloud+ increases those limits. Now we have a real-world example of what it looks like when limits are hit, and details on what counts toward those limits.

Here’s how Siri AI usage limits will work in iOS 27.3

Siri AI and select other AI features will begin having usage limits in iOS 27.3 for advanced tasks. 

This is standard practice with other AI services like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude because these tools rely on server-based models rather than running entirely on-device.

Here’s an example from the iOS 27.3 beta showing what it looks like when you hit your Siri AI daily usage limit. Per Ben in a post on X:

In a follow-up post, Ben clarifies that complex questions did stop working shortly after posting. As expected though, basic requests continued to work as usual—they don’t have a usage limit.

One question that Apple hasn’t made clear is what qualifies as a complex or “advanced” Siri AI request. The company shares just two examples of something advanced:

“Text Mark the address for Annika’s party, and tell him what time we need to leave from home to make it on time.”

“Add a summary of my San Francisco trip note to this email draft.”

	

But leaker pdfu has discovered exactly the instructions Siri AI follows to determine whether a request counts as basic or advanced. In a post on X he outlines the parameters for requests deemed “advanced.” 

Siri AI will check the request against this list, and if it involves any of these, it’s deemed “advanced.”

uses information from one app, from what is on screen or from a message, in a different app, or needs a result from one step used in a different step or app (such as a looked-up fact typed into a field)

contains two or more separate asks in one sentence, even in the same app (extra details of one action, such as a cc or a time, are still one ask)

asks about or summarizes the content of a photo, a camera view or an attachment (editing, searching and albums are fine)

deletes, archives, junks, moves, marks or changes a set (all, every, these or a whole category) of the user’s emails, notes, reminders, messages, photos, files, contacts or events

sets a device action or a notification to run on a time or trigger (not alarms, timers, reminders or calendar events), notifies someone when a person arrives or leaves, or builds or edits a Shortcut or automation

is deep research or a multi-step task done on the user’s behalf

asks you to compose or create new content (a story, poem, essay, plan, recipe, image, or an email or message from a topic rather than wording the user gives), or to rewrite in a tone other than friendly, professional or concise

It would be helpful if Apple publicly documented these guidelines for users. But perhaps after iOS 27.3 ships and usage limits are fully implemented, we’ll get more detail from the company.

What do you think of Siri AI’s parameters for advanced requests in iOS 27.3? Let us know in the comments.

title: Best Buy brings back 4K Blu-ray discs with an expanding collection, in-store availability [U]
snippet: It’s been nearly three years since Best Buy decided to ditch selling physical copies of movies, stripping its inventory from both its brick-and-mortar stores and its online catalog. But with the growing rise of 4K Blu-ray collections as a vinyl-esque collector’s item, the electronics giant has slowly begun dipping its toes back into the physical media game. more…
fullText:
It’s been nearly three years since Best Buy decided to ditch selling physical copies of movies, stripping its inventory from both its brick-and-mortar stores and its online catalog. But with the growing rise of 4K Blu-ray collections as a vinyl-esque collector’s item, the electronics giant has slowly begun dipping its toes back into the physical media game.

As spotted by TheHDRoom on Twitter and on the 4K Blu-ray subreddit, Best Buy is now selling 14 different 4K Blu-rays on its website, marking another step in the brand’s slow return to selling physical media. These films include:

The Odyssey

Project Hail Mary

Interstellar

Saving Private Ryan

Obsession

Top Gun/Top Gun: Maverick two-pack

White Christmas

Speed Racer (2008)

The Super Mario Galaxy Movie

The Godfather

It’s a Wonderful Life

Supergirl (2026)

Masters of the Universe (2026)

Dr. Seuss’ How the Grinch Stole Christmas (2000)

Technically, Blu-ray returned to Best Buy’s online storefront in August of 2025, when it opened a third-party marketplace similar to Amazon or Walmart. These titles, however, are shipped and sold by Best Buy. Everything’s still online-only, unfortunately, save for The Odyssey, which launched in-store shelf displays alongside yesterday’s release date. It shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise that The Odyssey is getting some special treatment; in addition to its status as a box office juggernaut, Nolan’s previous movie, Oppenheimer, initially sold out of physical copies in its first week of release in 2023. 

Outside of these 14 titles, additional Blu-rays continue to be sold through Best Buy’s third-party marketplace.

	

Update, 11/20: Best Buy confirmed to The HD Room on Twitter that The Odyssey is just the first 4K Blu-ray to return to physical locations, as it plans to continue adding “some” Blu-rays back to its stores.

The Odyssey may/will be joined by other 4K UHD titles at Best Buy in the future: 

"The Odyssey inspired a homecoming of our own – some physical media is returning to Best Buy. Sometimes what’s old does become new (again). And we're still feeling nostalgic, so stay tuned." pic.twitter.com/wz9xhcdo4G

— TheHDRoom in 4K UHD (@thehdroom) November 20, 2026

title: Trump endorses Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia, says US has no evidence of wrongdoing
snippet: The president cited the U.S. attorney general in defending Huang's return, while urging Nvidia to continue its export-control investigation.
fullText:
President Trump praised Nvidia’s decision on Monday to reinstate founder Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, saying on his social network Truth Social that “the United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security.”

The Nvidia board’s statement had also referred to consultations with “senior levels of the United States government” as informing its decision. It said that, based on that input, Mr. Huang’s reinstatement was deemed not a national security risk. 

In his comments on Monday, Trump claimed that U.S. Attorney General [Todd Blanche] had found no evidence that Mr. Huang had engaged in unlawful conduct. It’s an unusual statement for a U.S. president to make, as the attorney general typically conducts those investigations independently. Notably, Attorney General Blanche has not yet made a formal statement on the case.

There’s also indication that President Trump may have been aware of the decision before the announcement by the Nvidia board. Speaking to a PBS journalist over the weekend, he said of Huang “he’s back where he should be and we see he did absolutely nothing wrong.” Asked to clarify about whether he meant Huang would be reinstated, Trump said, “I hope so, I hope so.”

Huang was accused of having multiple extramarital relationships, including one with a direct report at Nvidia and another unnamed employee. However, the affair of most concern was the one with the alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (no relation). Ms. Huang was an executive at a Singapore-based company called Megaspeed, which had purchased billions in Nvidia chips over the past couple of years. This relationship had raised national security concerns about whether the CEO ties to Ms. Huang could have compromised sensitive information or facilitated China’s access to advanced U.S. AI chips, which are subject to export restrictions.

Trump said last week that he believed this relationship didn’t threaten the U.S.’s national security, and instead said that no one had proven she’s a spy. “She may not be a spy,” the president said, adding that “China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”

Trump’s full statement on Huang’s return, released on Monday, is below. 

The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The Country needs Jensen’s leadership at NVIDIA in order to ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy. The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to NVIDIA poses any risk to National Security. The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct. On a personal note, I have gotten to know Jensen, and he is a Great Patriot and National Treasure. Separately, NVIDIA should continue its thorough internal investigation of the Company’s compliance with U.S. export controls in order to ensure that it is fulfilling its legal obligations and Patriotic Duty to protect U.S. National Security. Congratulations to Jensen, the NVIDIA Board, to the People of the United States — and, indeed, the World! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP

title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
snippet: The stunning reversal was supported by senior officials in the U.S. government.
fullText:
In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy.

The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.

Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET.

In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security. 

Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity.

A long list of high-profile tech executives were pushing the board — in social media posts and publicly aired interviews — to bring Huang back, including SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, Atoms founder Travis Kalanick, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan — all of whom signed a petition pushing for reinstatement.

The company said the board’s unanimous decision followed a series of discussions and meetings with Huang, after which they were “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.”

Just a few days ago, the board had seemed immovable in its choice to push Huang out. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Nvidia board chair Harvey C. Jones said they didn’t intend to reinstate Huang. Nvidia had even retained executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.

Jones, along with the rest of the board, now has a different view. In a prepared statement, Jones said the board believes Huang is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of its stockholders, employees, partners, and customers.

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company,” Jones said. “We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia’s Chief Financial Officer.”

In a statement, Huang said he was honored to return to his role as the head of the company he co-founded in 1993.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said. “I want to thank the Nvidia Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading Nvidia during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Apple @ Work is exclusively brought to you by Mosyle, the only Apple Unified Platform. If you ask any Mac admin for a list of the software on their fleet, they’ll pull up their device management inventory and show you the apps they’ve deployed. Ask them what their developers installed with Homebrew last month, which VS Code extensions they are running, or what npm pulled into a project on Tuesday, and you’ll get a different response. Workbrew 2.0 treats that gap as a problem worth solving for IT teams.

About Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers has been an Apple IT admin since 2009. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade WiFi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train users, share stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

The software your device management server can’t see

Device management is built around the software IT deploys. Apps from Apple Business Manager, apps preloaded via your device management vendors’ packages, packages you upload, and profiles you push out. That model solves the problem for native macOS apps. It doesn’t cover what happens when the Mac becomes the default developer machine. Developers install what they need with a single command in Terminal, and Homebrew alone has more than 16,000 packages. You then add millions of npm packages and hundreds of thousands of IDE extensions, and the list of software on a Mac that IT didn’t put there is longer than the list it did.

That used to be a developer-only problem. It isn’t anymore, in the vibe-coding era. AI tools have turned marketers, analysts, and ops people into builders, and those builders install packages too.

Workbrew 2.0

Workbrew started as a management layer for Homebrew: an agent that reports what’s installed, flags known vulnerabilities, and lets IT push updates across the fleet. Version 2.0 expands the catalog to include npm packages, VS Code extensions, and macOS apps, all in a single inventory. The company says it has patched more than 10 million vulnerabilities for customers since its launch, and it’s now ISO 27001-certified.

The part that is critical for everyone who isn’t a developer is the new Workbrew app, a native Mac app for finding, installing, and updating approved software. Workbrew calls it “the app store for your entire company.” Employees can browse what IT has approved, install it without opening Terminal, and request anything that isn’t on the list. IT approves or denies in the Workbrew Console, and if it’s a no, the employee gets an answer on why.

The app comes from the Updatest team, which Workbrew acquired as part of this release. Updatest is the indie Mac app that keeps thousands of users’ software up to date, and it remains a separate product for individuals and families. For business customer, that experience is now the Workbrew app, and it’s included on every plan, including the free Team plan with no device or user limits.

With Workbrew, we finally have real visibility into what developers are using in Homebrew. Fleet-wide updates are effortless, and the team stays secure without being slowed down.

Chris Merrell, Director of IT, End User Services, Camping World

Where it fits next to your device management system

Workbrew isn’t a device management tool and isn’t trying to be one. Your device management system deploys the Workbrew agent, and Workbrew handles software your device management system lacks visibility into. If your fleet consists entirely of office workers on managed apps, there’s nothing here for you. If you have developers, or you’ve noticed the marketing team installing things to run AI scripts, you have the problem whether you’ve discovered it or not.

Wrap up

AI tools have changed how we think about app management, because apps get installed differently now. Workbrew 2.0 provides IT with a list of development tools on the Mac and gives employees a sanctioned way to get what they need.
