title: Honor just supercharged its smartwatch lineup with a new Pro model
snippet: The Honor Watch 6 Pro has a 5,500-nit OLED display, ceramic bezel, 18-day battery life, and costs less than it looks. more…
fullText:
The Honor Watch 6 Pro has a 5,500-nit OLED display, ceramic bezel, 18-day battery life, and costs less than it looks.

In the world of athletic smartwatches, it isn’t often that you could mistake one for a luxury watch, but Honor seems to want to flip all that on its head with the Honor Watch 6 Pro. Just take a look at this excerpt from the company’s press release:

Framing this brilliant display is a Precision Nanocrystalline Ceramic bezel crafted through a 1400°C high-temperature integrated sintering process, delivering a delicate texture and rich visual depth.

Inspired by modernist architecture, its diamond-cut octagonal rotatable crown features a dual-layer horizontal and vertical cut, complemented by a side button for intuitive navigation.

That sounds pretty wild to me, and it’s backed up by specs that sound just as legit, too. On top is a 1.5-inch LTPO Tandem AMOLED display that outputs 5,500-nit peak brightness. Underneath is a bevy of new sensors called the Intelligent Sense System, which Honor says combines “multi-wavelength monitoring, multi-optical path patrol technology, and anti-interference glass technology to reach deep skin layers.”

Pre-sales begin today at €279/£229 for early bird pricing.

Runners will be pleased to know that the Honor Watch 6 Pro not only incorporates a dual-band GPS, but combines it with a “star-pointing 3-antenna design” and an AI fusion algorithm, which should deliver ultra-accurate tracking in any location and no matter how you hold your wrist. Despite its luxury looks, this one tracks over 120 sports modes, including Honor’s Professional Running Coach feature, which tracks running posture, lactate threshold, heart rate targets, and keeps you on pace with real-time voice coaching.

	

During sports modes like Badminton, the watch can identify more than six types of swings, and Honor says other sports modes can deliver similarly detailed statistics. The watch is 5ATM, IP68, IP69, and IP69K water-and-dust-resistant rated, plus it integrates directly with Strava so you can pull all your fitness data together.

Honor is incorporating a new wrist twist gesture system this time around, letting you use gestures to perform actions hands-free. The watch is rated at 10 days of battery life on a single charge in regular usage mode, while endurance mode will stretch that to 18 days. Pre-sales begin today, November 19, and run until December 31, when the watch is expected to launch, starting at €279/£229 for early bird pricing. After launch, the retail MSRP starts at €379/£329.

title: Google Gemini Partners With Watch Duty to Clear Static From Firefighter Radio
snippet: After spending months training with firefighters in the field, the app uses Google Gemini to decode distorted radio signals in real time.
fullText:
On Friday, Google’s Gemini team announced the results of a new partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders. The results cut vital new wildfire dispatch translations down to seconds and helped improve radio communications, which can be rough on the front lines of a new fire.

The Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert. The alert stemmed from a nearly unintelligible, static-filled 911 call that the Gemini tool transcribed in under 30 seconds. That kind of assistance can help Watch Duty send alerts to affected communities more quickly and enable first responders to update maps more accurately and make better-informed decisions.

“This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” said Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty. “Across disasters, we hear feedback every day that first responders are using Watch Duty for additional situational awareness, especially for disasters that span multiple counties.” 

			

More from CNET

Watch Duty reporters are active and retired first responders who can manually monitor up to 20 different feeds, though static and rapid-fire jargon can make them difficult to follow.

Gemini workers used more than 20,000 hours of Watch Duty radio recordings to train the AI tool to recognize firefighting terms that aren’t in the average dictionary or books that AIs are typically trained on.

Google says the tool is not designed to replace human decision-making in life-or-death situations. 

“This tool takes on the demanding work of listening, freeing Watch Duty’s volunteers to focus on what matters most: confirming fires and getting warnings to people while they can still act,” said Stephanie Chew, Google project team lead.

The project was completed at no cost thanks to a Google.org fellowship, and the resulting Watch Duty app features are free to use.

Improving real-world fire alerts and transcriptions

Reducing the time it takes to understand radio dispatches is only one advantage of the Gemini tool.Watch Duty/CNET

From the data collected, Gemini engineers and Watch Duty identified several measures of success.

One metric was the word error rate, which fell by around 15% after the AI model was implemented. Another sign of success was a jump in Watch Duty volunteers’ satisfaction with their radio transcription tools, from around 35% to 92%.

The Gemini tool continues to analyze approximately 200 hours of radio speech traffic from 400 feeds per day. The tool was made to handle more than 10,000 radio feeds if necessary.

The integration could pave the way for broader use across public safety. The platform’s built-in scalability could eventually bring similar audio-clearing tools to local fire departments, 911 call centers and Coast Guard operations, where clear communication is critical under pressure.

Among iOS 27’s many new features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets dual iPhone users keep the same phone number across devices

With iOS 27, Apple introduces big AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting new features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the update also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:

After iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

Most users will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

	

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”

So far carrier support is limited (here’s the latest list), but Apple plans to expand iPhone Handoff to more carriers soon.

Do you have a need to use the same phone number on multiple iPhones? For what reason? Let us know in the comments.

title: AirPods Pro 3 were worth the upgrade for one standout feature
snippet: AirPods Pro 3 (now only $149, down from $249) offer many advantages over AirPods Pro 2, but after a year of use, the improvements to Active Noise Cancellation alone have proven worth the upgrade. more…
fullText:
AirPods Pro 3 (now only $149, down from $249) offer many advantages over AirPods Pro 2, but after a year of use, the improvements to Active Noise Cancellation alone have proven worth the upgrade.

Apple doubled Active Noise Cancellation in AirPods Pro 3, and it’s been a huge upgrade

I’ve been using AirPods Pro 3 for over a year, and they had a lot to live up to because I already loved AirPods Pro 2 so much. Initially I found the new ear tips less comfortable, but thankfully that issue went away after a little extra time.

Some highlights of AirPods Pro 3 include the longer battery life, with 8 hours per charge compared to 6 on the previous model. The charging case’s new Ultra Wideband chip also makes it easier to find when it’s lost. Some users will appreciate the heart rate sensor, but I wear an Apple Watch all the time so it doesn’t benefit me much.

These new features are nice to have, but Active Noise Cancellation is where AirPods Pro 3 become a major upgrade. Apple says it’s “the world’s best in-ear Active Noise Cancellation.” Here’s how the new ANC compares to previous models:

removes up to 2x more noise than AirPods Pro 2

removes up to 4x more noise than AirPods Pro

I spend nearly my entire workday with AirPods Pro 3 in my ears. Whether I’m working from home with young kids around or at a busy coffee shop, I rely on ANC to block out background noise and help me focus.

One reason I’ve been especially impressed with the ANC upgrades is that I didn’t have any real complaints about ANC on AirPods Pro 2. But Apple managed to deliver improvements in AirPods Pro 3 I had no idea I needed, and when I’ve tried going back to AirPods Pro 2 I couldn’t believe how much noise was let in.

If Active Noise Cancellation is important to you, I highly recommend AirPods Pro 3.

Highlights

In short, this app replicates the Samsung Frame TV experience but for anyone who owns an Apple TV. As mentioned above, you can choose from over 1000 hand-picked art pieces to choose from the world’s museums, but you can also import your own photos from iCloud.

title: Not upgrading to iPhone 18 Pro or Duo? Here’s what’s coming in 2027
snippet: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year. more…
fullText:
iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year.

2027 is going to be a relatively big iPhone release year for Apple. First, the company will be continuing the iPhone 18 lineup after it introduced a split release schedule. Then, in the fall, the company will debut a new round of flagships in celebration of the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. Here’s what to expect.

Spring 2027

iPhone 18

For the first time, Apple will be introducing its base iPhone in the spring. Upgrades for the iPhone 18 aren’t quite clear, though more RAM is one of the key rumors. Thermal upgrades will likely happen as well, as well as the new Apple C2 modem.

It’s possible Apple will update the design to fall more in line with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, though we don’t yet know.

This phone will of course equip the A20 chip, and it’ll probably start at the same $899 price point that iPhone 17 currently sits at – after it was increased from $799 in September.

iPhone 18e

This phone will most likely just end up being a chip bump from the A19 to A20 chip, and debut in the Spring alongside the iPhone 18. Earlier this year, reports indicated that Apple would share many components between the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, though it isn’t quite clear what that could mean for the devices.

iPhone Air 2

Out of all of the spring iPhone releases, this one is the one to look forward to. After receiving a lukewarm reception with the initial iPhone Air model, Apple went back to the drawing board and decided to modify the design to fit an ultrawide camera into the device.

Personally, I don’t think an ultrawide camera is too important – though many people will see one camera on the back of the phone and immediately assume it’s less premium, so it’ll probably end up being an important upgrade for the sake of sales. Plus, ultrawide photos can be fun at times.

It should also have a larger battery, reportedly as large as 3500mAh. That’s a roughly 10% improvement from the original iPhone Air. iPhone Air 2 will likely also jump from Apples C1X modem to the C2.

Fall 2027

iPhone 20 Pro

For the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, Apple is expected to debut a fully redesigned iPhone to celebrate. It’ll reportedly be much more glassy, feature significantly slimmer bezels, a quad curved display, and ditch the flat edge design of the iPhone 12 and later. 

Personally, I’m slightly skeptical that this’ll truly be a replacement to the “Pro” phone for thermal reasons, but time will tell. iPhone Duo seemingly has strong thermals while not featuring an aluminum unibody, so my concern might not be relevant. It’ll offer two, larger display sizes: 6.4-inch and 7-inch. This largely comes from the bezel reduction.

	

If you’re holding out for iPhone 18 Pro, this “iPhone 20” is definitely the phone to wait out for.

iPhone Duo 2

Lastly, Apple will release a successor to its just-announced iPhone Duo next fall. Of course, you can expect next-generation Apple Silicon with the A21 Pro chip next year, but there aren’t many other substantial changes expected. Apple may bring proper Face ID to the outer display, an improvement from the recently-announced face unlock, but it’s unclear whether this feature will make the engineering cutoff date.

title: TechCrunch Mobility: A/B testing robots vs. humans
snippet: Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and, now more than ever, the role AI is playing in it.
fullText:
Welcome back to TechCrunch Mobility, your hub for the future of transportation and, now more than ever, the role AI is playing in it. To get this in your inbox, sign up here for free — just click TechCrunch Mobility!

Waymo pulling its robotaxis off freeways (again) and Zoox robotaxis launching on the Uber app illustrate the push and pull between progress and setbacks in the autonomous vehicle industry. 

There are signs of growth. For instance, Tesla has now surpassed Waymo in Texas in the number of robotaxis registered with the state (Tesla has 1,507 and Waymo has 1,345). But does that translate to market dominance? 

A better metric, if we’re trying to gauge who is leading, would be commercial driverless miles. And if we’re measuring cost-efficiency, another useful metric would be driverless miles per vehicle. By those measures, Waymo is still ahead, based on data available to me. But with Waymo’s recent freeways setback and Tesla’s push to expand its robotaxi fleet with Cybercabs, that lead could shrink. 

Not that there needs to be a winner, by the way. Transportation is deeply fragmented, and there is room for multiple players in the U.S., not to mention the rest of the world. 

A/B test: humans vs. robots 

A recent discussion with my Autonocast co-host Ed Niedermeyer, whose book, “Elon Take the Wheel,” comes out December 1, got me thinking about how Las Vegas could soon become a real world A/B test of sorts for human-driven vs. autonomous ride-hailing services. 

Uber, as mentioned above, just added Zoox to its ride-hailing app in Las Vegas. For now, riders don’t have much of a choice. Uber customers can increase their chances of getting a Zoox robotaxi, and they can always decline a robot ride. But they can’t directly select a robotaxi. Instead, Uber riders will be matched with one if it’s available. 

Uber said that will soon change. The company plans to introduce a dedicated autonomous option in its app as “availability and reliability improve,” Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call in November. 

Las Vegas will also become the first U.S. city where riders can access two fully driverless partners through the Uber app, he said. (Hyundai’s self-driving subsidiary Motional is also an Uber partner.)

That would give Uber riders a meaningful choice: a human driver or a robotaxi, and potentially even which autonomous service to use. And it could offer a revealing look at what customers actually prefer when given that choice. Price could tip the balance, too. 

It makes me wonder whether Las Vegas will become the next battleground for organized labor as robotaxis begin competing directly with human drivers.

A little bird

Image Credits:Bryce Durbin

You might have seen the Wall Street Journal scoop that General Motors is working with an executive search firm to identify possible candidates to replace CEO Mary Barra. Rumors of her imminent departure have swirled for months, but this time there appears to be real work happening behind the scenes. 

I reached out to a few little birds to learn more and here’s what they’re telling me. And, for the record, GM declined to comment. 

GM has hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles, according to one source, who noted it’s possible that the board has other executive search firms working on this as well. The board is taking a two-track approach to its search, which is occurring simultaneously. 

The first is focused on traditional yet transformative automotive CEOs. One name that has come up from the executive search firm is José Muñoz, who is president and CEO of Hyundai. The board is also interested in someone less traditional. The firm has apparently floated names like Doug Field, who recently became CEO of Mind Robotics, and Larry Culp of GE, according to a source with direct information. 

There are internal GM folks who are also in the mix, including Sterling Anderson, co-founder of self-driving trucks company Aurora who became chief product officer at GM in May 2025, and Paul Jacobson, the company’s executive vice president and chief financial officer.

Got a tip for us? Email Kirsten Korosec at [email protected]. 

Deals!

Image Credits:Bryce Durbin

Elysian Aircraft, the Dutch aerospace company developing aviation electrification technologies, raised €12 million in private and public funding from FideFlux, SecFund, and ROM InWest, as well as from individual investors and family offices.

Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, an electric three-wheeler business under Mahindra & Mahindra, is looking at an IPO in about 18 months, per Bloomberg.  

Numa, a startup developing an AI operating system for dealerships, raised a $45 million Series C round led by New York-based Blue Cloud Ventures. Threshold Ventures, Costanoa, Touring Capital, Gradient Ventures, and Tokio Marine Future Fund also participated. 

Stark Future, a European electric motorcycle company, raised at least €150 million in equity, Reuters reported. The raise was led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management’s 1GT and Axon Partners Group. 

Vincue, an automotive tech company that sells software to dealerships, raised $93 million in a round led by Wavecrest Growth Partners, with continued backing from FM Capital.

Notable reads and other tidbits

Image Credits:Bryce Durbin

Also, the electric micromobility startup that spun out of Rivian last year, has paused deliveries of its new e-bike over problems with its software and batteries, The Verge reported. 

Edmunds released new data that found the average new vehicle is selling for a record $50,087.

Redwood Materials is using computer vision and machine learning to identify and sort batteries by chemistry before they’re fed into the company’s rotary calciner — a massive cylindrical industrial furnace used to process 40,000 metric tons of raw feedstock a year. 

Tesla said it will spend about $3.3 billion to expand its Berlin gigafactory to produce Cybercabs — yet another signal of the company’s global autonomy ambitions. 

Over the weekend, Tesla invited “select customers” to preorder the company’s autonomous, golden Cybercab “for personal use.” The Cybercab is priced at $29,990, but there is a lot more to ownership. The company will charge owners $299 a month to use the vehicles, delivery will only occur in a handful of cities, and operations will be limited to specific locations.

Uber opened its ride-hailing service to children as young as 10 in three U.S. cities. Uber already has a service for teenagers. If this program proves successful, it would open Uber up to another market of customers: busy families. 

Meanwhile, Uber said it’s notifying close to 150,000 drivers that their personal information was stolen in an October data breach. 

Zipline continues to scale its autonomous drone delivery business, this time in its partnership with Uber. The companies had previously announced a partnership for drones to deliver for Uber Eats, but it officially launched this week in a Houston suburb. The aim is a big one: Uber and Zipline say they aim to make 1 million deliveries a day using the startup’s drones by the end of 2029.

One more thing …

I had a chance to catch up with (and interview) Ro Gupta, the head of Woven Capital — Toyota’s growth fund.

I’ve known Gupta for years; we first met when I worked at Fortune and he had a startup called Carmera. A lot has happened since those AV 1.0 days, and Gupta caught us up on this next era of AV innovation and where Toyota is interested in investing. It’s not enough to simply state “AI.” There’s more to it than that. Take a listen.

title: ChatGPT app gains enhanced Live Dictation streaming without 10-minute limit
snippet: ChatGPT dictation is getting a boost today. OpenAI has updated the speech-to-text feature with Live Dictation that improves both speed and reliability. The enhanced dictation update also removes the 10-minute limit. more…
fullText:
ChatGPT dictation is getting a boost today. OpenAI has updated the speech-to-text feature with Live Dictation that improves both speed and reliability. The enhanced dictation update also removes the 10-minute limit.

“Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable,” OpenAI announced on X.

“With Live Dictation, your speech turns into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for your message to finish transcribing,” the company continued. 

Atty Eleti, who works on voice features at OpenAI, added that the 10-minute dictation limit has also been removed as part of the dictation streaming upgrade.

More details from today’s app update release notes below:

Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable.

With Live Dictation, your speech turns into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for your message to finish transcribing. Tap or click on the waveform to show or hide text as you go. We’ve also removed the 10-minute recording limit.

Live Dictation is rolling out globally to all ChatGPT plans on iOS, Android, web, and the desktop app.

title: Trump reportedly called into Nvidia board meeting to advocate for Huang’s return
snippet: "I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them," the president told CNBC.
fullText:
A close ally of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, President Donald Trump reportedly dialed into an Nvidia board meeting to push for the ousted CEO’s return, Semafor reported on Monday. Trump got his way, as Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement shortly afterward.

“I spoke to them, let me put it that way … And I convinced them,” the president told CNBC.

Huang was forced to step down from his role as CEO, which he held for 33 years, after news broke that he had affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees, including a direct report.

“President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” White House communications director Steven Cheung told Semafor.

The president took to his social media app, Truth Social, to remark that “the United States government has no reason to believe that Jensen’s return to Nvidia poses any risk to national security.”

According to Nvidia’s press release about Huang’s reinstatement as CEO and president, the company claimed that “the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

While Trump has declared that Huang “did absolutely nothing wrong,” many government officials aren’t buying the president’s point of view. Huang is still expected to testify in closed-door conversations with three committees of the House of Representatives on December 1. He is also slated to appear before the Senate Banking Committee to testify publicly, though that hearing has not been scheduled yet.

“People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it’s a threat to lose him,” Trump said to CNBC.

Trump has maintained this position through the scandal, even denying that he was ever told about Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang (no relation). The New York Times reported, on the contrary, that Trump’s secretary of state and national security adviser Marco Rubio briefed him aboard Air Force One in May.

Earlier this spring, Rubio also supervised the drafting of a memo that circulated among top policymakers, warning that Alice Huang was spying for China’s Ministry of State Security.

title: Apple Watch Series 12: Four standout features make me glad I upgraded
snippet: I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did. more…
fullText:
I upgraded to an Apple Watch Series 12 this fall (now $329 on Amazon), and there are four main features that make me especially glad I did.

#1: S11 chip makes everything fast

The Apple Watch was overdue for a chip update, with Apple skipping any changes last year and not having any true performance upgrades since the S9.

I’m happy to report that the new S11 chip appears much faster and more capable than its predecessor, the S10.

Everyday tasks on Apple Watch Series 12 just feel fast. And Siri AI, a tentpole addition in watchOS 27, very much feels made for this latest hardware. Siri was sluggish on older hardware in my testing, but it performs much more like I’d hoped on Series 12.

#2: New health features and complications

The new Health Sensing System makes Apple Watch Series 12 better at tracking key metrics like heart rate and steps. But this isn’t a case where accuracy is the only improvement.

Because of the new health sensors, Series 12 offers three complications not available before:

Heart Rate

Daily Steps

Readiness

The complications let you see up-to-date readings on your current heart rate, step count, and readiness score right from your watch face. These are very welcome additions that meaningfully improve the Apple Watch’s health and wellness feature set.

#3: Siri Recap

I’ve been using the watchOS 27.3 beta, which adds a new Siri Recap feature for Series 12 models that I really love.

Here’s what it does per Apple:

Siri Recap ambiently takes notes on your conversations throughout your day and creates high-level Apple Intelligence–generated summaries that you can use later to jog your memory, so you can stay present in the moment.

Most of what Siri documents, I’ll never need to reference and it gets deleted automatically. But for those times I have trouble remembering a key piece of information, I’ve found Siri Recap a very convenient addition.

#4: Faster charging

Apple Watch Series 12 offers largely the same battery life as Series 11, though it will last 25% longer for outdoor workouts.

More battery is always nice, but I’m especially a fan of the faster charging available on Series 12. Here’s how it stacks up to Series 11:

Apple Watch Series 12: 15 minutes charge gets up to 12 hours battery life

Apple Watch Series 11: 15 minutes charge gets up to 8 hours battery life

I wear my Apple Watch to bed and generally try to top it off quickly in the evening, but I’m not always great at giving it much time on the charger. With faster charging support on Series 12, my poor planning isn’t a problem.

title: Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver
snippet: No space agency has ever staged spacecraft in orbit for a year before sending them on to Mars.
fullText:
NASA launched its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

It’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

Typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice. 

			

More from CNET

The other big win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water. 

Another 10 months flying through space

The Hohmann Transfer uses gravity and orbits to get spacecraft to Mars without using massive amounts of fuel.NASA

Escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their new trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally shows up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year. 

By the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

This is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally launched Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and launched themselves into outer space.

The Mars launch window

The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient. 

“With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a new strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, said in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”

The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, launched its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons. 

Despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX launched, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO With the US Government’s Blessing
snippet: The decision was made with “input from senior levels of the United States government,” according to the board.
fullText:
Nvidia announced on Monday that ousted cofounder Jensen Huang would return to his role as CEO after he resigned earlier this month when multiple extramarital affairs became public, including one with a woman that the US intelligence community believes is a Chinese intelligence asset.

“The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, chair of Nvidia’s board. “We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the company.”

The stunning news comes after weeks of reporting on alleged malfeasance in Huang’s personal and professional lives. The scandal broke when The New York Times reported that Huang had a close, personal relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. Then came news of a second extramarital affair, leading to Huang’s eventual resignation.

			

More from CNET

Previously, the board denied it would bring Huang back, despite Huang saying he would return if the board allowed it. Many names were floated as a possible replacement for Huang, including Arm CEO Rene Haas. But many tech experts said it was difficult to imagine Nvidia without Huang. Apparently, the board agreed.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress temporarily took over as interim CEO, telling investors at its recent earnings call that everything is “business as usual.” But additional reporting revealed that Huang regularly “humiliated” his direct reports, raising serious questions about his management style and the corporate culture of Nvidia, which Huang helped shape more than any other person over the past 20 years.

Nvidia’s stock price rose dramatically on Monday morning with the news of Huang’s return, dragging with it other chipmakers like AMD and Qualcomm and market indices including the S&P 500, Nasdaq and Dow, which all jumped up on Monday. It’s another sign that Nvidia, as a key company in the AI industry, is a driving force behind the US and global economy.

The board added that it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” on the decision. President Donald Trump said in a Truth Social post that Nvidia made the “correct and proper decision” to reinstate Huang, adding, “The Attorney General of the United States has confirmed that the US Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.”

The board’s independently commissioned investigation into Huang will continue, but he will regain his seat on the board. Huang is still set to testify before the Senate’s banking committee on Dec. 3, and the SEC’s investigation into Nvidia is also still set to continue.

Trump on Huang: ‘We have to protect our geniuses’

Calling into CNBC’s Squawk Box on Monday morning, Trump reiterated that Huang’s return is good news for the country. He called Huang a “genius,” saying, “We have to protect our geniuses … The bigger threat is losing the brainpower of a person like Jensen.” In a rambling interview, Trump talked about the importance of Nvidia’s industry-leading chips.

Trump previously floated the idea of former Apple CEO Tim Cook taking over Nvidia’s top job, which gained zero traction. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been pushing for further scrutiny of Huang and Nvidia’s compliance with US export control rules. While Trump loosened the rules around how US chipmakers can do business with Chinese companies, there are still bans on selling the most advanced chips.

But we need only look to the stock market to see why the Trump administration may be changing its tune. Since the beginning of the scandal, Nvidia’s stock price has fallen dramatically, wiping out billions in market value. Monday morning’s news of Huang’s return saw premarket trading hike its share price by 30%. With Nvidia, so goes the entire stock market. And after last week’s Anthropic IPO failed to quell concerns over a growing “AI bubble” — where Nvidia is smack-dab in the center — the rebound points to investors’ confidence in Huang, Nvidia and the AI industry, spies and affairs be damned.

What this tells us about the AI industry’s future

Within Silicon Valley, some have continually pushed for Huang’s return. Elon Musk posted an ominous “It is done” on Monday morning; Epic CEO Tim Sweeney posted a link to AC/DC’s Back in Black, a nod to Huang’s affinity for expensive black leather jackets.

The tech industry, perhaps more than any other, thrives on the narrative of the god-like startup founder. It’s why Jensen Huang was synonymous with Nvidia, Sam Altman with OpenAI and Dario Amodei with Anthropic. And this is not the first time a major tech CEO’s departure has caused such a commotion.

“[Huang’s] return may help restore investor confidence, but the upheaval echoes Sam Altman’s brief ouster and reinstatement at OpenAI,” Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne said, “raising similar questions about corporate governance and the outsized influence of individual leaders over the future of AI.”

Altman was fired and reinstated within a chaotic five-day period in 2023. The OpenAI board accused Altman of lying to them, but he was ultimately welcomed back and has kept a firm grip on the now-huge AI company ever since. This episode is the basis for Luca Guadagnino’s upcoming movie, Artificial, starring Andrew Garfield as Altman, coming out next month.

Those tech founders have become increasingly intertwined with government power, particularly since Trump’s return to office. Many Big Tech executives, including Huang, have donated billions in personal funds for Trump’s projects, such as his inauguration fund and plans for a White House ballroom. It’s led many tech critics to argue that Big Tech is buying influence to avoid regulation and oversight.

“​For years, Big Tech has used ‘national security’ as a pretext for killing pro-competition, kids’ privacy, and AI safety bills,” said Sacha Haworth, founder and CEO of the Tech Oversight Project. “But when their favorite CEO’s indiscretion helps a foreign rival, those concerns are thrown out the window in favor of protecting their own interests.” 

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Katelyn Chedraoui
						

						

							Reporter 2

Her work explores how new AI technology is infiltrating our lives, shaping the content we consume on social media and affecting the people behind the screens. title: Instagram finally lets users edit Stories after publishing, but there’s a catch
snippet: Every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days. more…
fullText:
Every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an update that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days.

No more deleting and reposting Stories

As spotted by The Verge, Instagram head Adam Mosseri confirmed today that the app will finally let users edit a Story after publishing.

This means users will be able to add stickers and drawings, fix typos or adjust text, and even change the music without having to delete the Story and publish it again, which would mean losing any views it had already received.

The catch is that users will only have 15 minutes after publishing a Story to make changes by tapping the ellipsis button at the bottom of the screen, and then selecting “Edit story.”

Here’s Mosseri’s post announcing the news:

Today’s update is the latest in a series of changes Instagram has made this year to address longstanding user requests.

Back in March, the app introduced the ability to reorder photos and videos in a carousel after publishing. In April, it added an option to edit comments (also within 15 minutes of posting), and in June, it began letting users manually rearrange posts on their profile grid.

More recently, Instagram also brought its free Edits video editor to the Mac, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, and 4K exports.

title: Don’t Miss Out on GTA 6 Launch Week: Here’s How to Take Rockstar’s New Game Anywhere
snippet: Whether you’re on a work trip, vacationing or otherwise indisposed, there are a few good options to scratch your Grand Theft Auto itch on the go.
fullText:
Look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Not everyone gets to write a review of the most anticipated video game in recent memory, or live blog their first 24 hours roaming around Vice City.

A lot of folks are still working away, daydreaming about getting back on the sticks and knocking off corner stores as Jason and Lucia right now. Some people are even on work trips or vacations away from their home consoles right now – let’s keep them in our thoughts.

But even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6. Sure, the game may currently be console-locked to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, but there are still clever ways to get the game booted up when you’re on the go.

			

More from CNET

Here’s everything you need to know about the remote play features that you’ll need to take this modern Bonnie and Clyde story on the road.

Whether you’re taking a flight to the real-life Vice City or you’re elsewhere in the world, there are still ways to play GTA 6.Rockstar Games

PS5 and Xbox Remote Play features will work with a console setup at home

So long as you have a PS5 or an Xbox with GTA 6 downloaded and ready to go, you can experience the game through smaller devices even when you’re away from home.

Both modern consoles support remote play, a feature that lets you stream your game from your home setup.

If you’re looking to turn on the Xbox’s remote play feature, you need to access the Profile & System settings in the Xbox guide. From there, you need to navigate to the Devices & Connections menu and choose the Remote features option.

You’ll need to enable the remote features and put your console into sleep mode in order to pair your chosen remote play device. Remote play devices include smartphones, tablets and Windows computers.

Gamers who own a PlayStation 5 will need to follow similar steps to get remote play functioning on a mobile device. Within the PlayStation’s settings menu, navigate to the System tab and choose Remote Play. Toggle the Enable Remote Play option. From there, all of the necessary device pairing and gameplay setup will happen through the PS Remote Play app, which you can download on your handheld device.

Whether you own a PlayStation or an Xbox, you’ll want to ensure your console settings are tuned so it stays connected to the internet in rest mode. You’ll also need to enable the console to turn on via a network connection. These settings will allow you to start a remote play session anytime, even if you’ve already left your home.

The controls for the PlayStation Portal are familiar and easy to grasp for fans of Sony’s home consoles.Scott Stein/CNET

Do some handheld heisting on the PlayStation Portal

If you’re using PlayStation’s remote play feature, you don’t have to fiddle around with gaming tablets or third-party handheld devices in order to find a comfortable way to play GTA 6. Sony’s PlayStation Portal is the perfect console accessory for natural gameplay, since it retains the DualShock controller design.

The PlayStation Portal connects to the PlayStation 5 for remote play the same way as any other device. It’s worth noting that the PlayStation Portal also allows PlayStation Plus Premium subscribers to access a limited library of cloud streaming titles – but this won’t help you with GTA 6. If you want to play Rockstar’s new game away from home, you still need to make sure to leave your console on before you leave the house.

If you’re forced to carry around a whole home console, I’d recommend the PlayStation 5 Slim (pictured right) for its lighter weight and thinner profile.Sean Booker/CNET

If all else fails, you’ll have to lug your console around

GTA 6 isn’t coming out on PC for a while still. That limits how many options you have when it comes to taking the game on the go with you. If (for whatever reason) you don’t have access to any remote play options, that leaves you with only the most inconvenient and unwieldy way to take the new crime simulator with you on the road.

You’ll have to lug around your PS5 or Xbox wherever you go to get in some GTA time – but hey, at least the gaming industry’s deteriorating respect for physical media means you won’t have to keep track of a disc.

The PS5 Slim is probably the easiest current-gen console to carry with you, since the digital edition weighs less than 6 pounds. But you’re giving up the best possible performance available on the PS5 Pro.

Either way, you’ll be carrying around a large, expensive piece of hardware, so this option should only be considered if you really can’t get remote play functioning for whatever reason.

Yes, you have to have a console for Xbox Cloud Gaming too

Microsoft’s video game ecosystem is huge, with Game Pass and streaming options available for PC players. But the Xbox brand isn’t offering gamers a cheat code to play GTA 6 on their beefy rigs (or any convenient handheld devices).

GTA 6 is only available on Xbox consoles with Xbox Cloud Gaming at this time. The upside is that this option lets you play the boundary-pushing new game on the Xbox One, which is very close to being two console generations old.

The bad news is that the value proposition of Xbox Cloud Gaming has become notably worse in recent months, as Microsoft did away with unlimited service for Game Pass subscribers. Even if you use this service to play GTA 6 on the go with your older console, you’ll get a maximum of 15 hours of playtime before you have to cough up more cash.

At that point, you’re better off biting the bullet on a current-generation console and considering the available remote play options.

title: I love YouTube on TV, but we desperately need better watchlist controls
snippet: Managing a YouTube watchlist shouldn’t be as frustrating as it is, especially on the most-used app in my life. Google’s premier streaming app has too many issues with resurfacing content; in my opinion, this is now a major problem that needs to be fixed. more…
fullText:
Managing a YouTube watchlist shouldn’t be as frustrating as it is, especially on the most-used app in my life. Google’s premier streaming app has too many issues with resurfacing content; in my opinion, this is now a major problem that needs to be fixed.

Aside from my YouTube watchlist gripes, it’s no secret that moving from a web browser to the TV is ultimately still a frustrating experience.

Lots of things I love about watching videos on my laptop or PC just don’t translate well to when I’m sat on my sofa holding a remote trying to find something to watch after wrapping up for the day. One thing I’m getting annoyed with is how YouTube scales on TV and Android TV boxes because you’re given less choice and arguably poorer recommendations for content due to the constraints in place.

Understandably, you can’t compress the layout too much on a TV as you’re typically sat a few feet away and all aspects of the interface need to be legible. I would still like to tweak it, though, if that were possible.

	

Maybe we could get proper sections for content, like how Netflix and other streaming platforms offer categorized areas where you can search for “comedy” or “horror”. I’m almost certain that, with Google’s insane investment and massive AI push, where every video is already analyzed hundreds of times, that wouldn’t be too difficult to do.

The problem now is that the sidebar menu is just too broad. Gaming covers basically everything. Then each line of videos accounts for one title, but requires search and previous watch data to populate. I find myself often fighting with recommendations on my TV, whereas on desktop it’s not as much of a problem.

That leads me to my biggest problem with YouTube, and it’s the, frankly, embarrassing watchlist or “Watch later” controls.

I can’t fault that it works, but right now the watchlist function is like something out of the early 2000s due to the lack of flexibility that I touched on above. As my YouTube consumption has increased 20x over the past four or five years, managing what I want to come back to or might have missed the first time around is starting to become a bit of a chore.

I’ve tried using playlists to save things, but things get messy very quickly because of how cumbersome it is to a) create a playlist on TV and b) how playlists are organized by default.

Google TV isn’t perfect, but it’s where I keep my biggest TV and movie watchlist outside of YouTube. Yes, YouTube is mostly for user-generated content, but I would take something as basic as Google TV’s interface baked into YouTube somehow. Add in categorization and auto-clear.

The Watch Later section has become an unwieldy place that I never really want to go unless I desperately have to. I’m constantly losing videos that I hoped to come back to or have an affinity for.

Videos don’t clear automatically, nor do you know when they were added. Yes, I’ll give credit that you can sort by a few options, but that’s the bare minimum. The process of moving things around is slow and takes multiple taps. Watch Later is also hidden compared to other services. It’s under your account, then beneath “Liked videos,” which is below any you may have uploaded yourself.

On a TV, the process is so annoying I just avoid it altogether. You go to the sidebar menu > Library > Watch later. It should be front-and-center on a TV. It’s almost unforgivable in my eyes because even your watch history is given greater prominence. I simply cannot understand that decision.

I’m not always a huge fan of AI being shoehorned into apps and services, but this is one of those areas that has been left to rot for a while and could get a big uplift from adding in a little bit of Gemini. Even if it were just an enhanced search function or more tools for organizing.

With YouTube TV effectively taking over regular broadcast television and being the world’s biggest streaming platform, I’m shocked by how so many areas of the platform remain in a consistently neglected state.

A little bit of spit and polish, and maybe I’ll start using this section again. For now, though, I’ll stick to texting myself links of stuff I want to watch. The ball is in your court, Google.

Still waiting for tech like the Vision Pro, but in normal everyday glasses and sunglasses? The industry leader in AR glasses shipments has something to say.

RayNeo isn’t a small player making a big claim here. The company took the No. 1 spot in global AR smart glasses shipments across the first half of 2026, with 24.8% market share according to IDC and 23.9% according to Counterpoint Research.

Turn your iPhone into a 307-inch screen with RayNeo GT Max — no headset required

Watching a movie on your iPhone is convenient, but craning your neck for a comfortable view is hardly cinematic. Having a premium AR display in sunglasses form, without packing a bulky mixed-reality headset or computing puck, opens up entirely new possibilities.

The RayNeo GT Max and RayNeo GT connect to your device over a single USB-C cable. Instead of clunky goggles, the GT Series puts a massive virtual display — 59 degrees of field of view on GT Max, to be exact — into a sleek, understated sunglasses design that blends into coffee shops and airport lounges at just 68 to 78 grams. That single USB-C connection carries uncompressed video and powers the glasses directly: no secondary battery packs to carry, no charging anxiety, and zero wireless lag.

One thing to check before you buy: the glasses need a device that outputs video over USB-C (DisplayPort Alt Mode). That covers the iPhone 15, 16 and 17 series, Macs from 2015 onward with USB-C, iPad from the 10th generation on, and USB-C handhelds like the Steam Deck. The iPhone 16e, 17e and iPhone Air have USB-C ports but don’t output video over them, so they aren’t supported. Consoles and older Lightning devices need RayNeo’s HDMI adapter.

Both GT Max and GT use dual 1080p Micro-OLED panels, delivering a Full HD image to each eye with ultra-smooth 120Hz refresh rates in 2D mode. GT Max adds 38 pixels per degree, 98% DCI-P3 cinematic color coverage, and TÜV Rheinland triple eye-comfort certification. GT Max’s wider field of view provides a more expansive picture, while GT offers a featherweight design. For travel, the appeal is simple: an immaculate 307-inch personal theater that slips right into your daily bag alongside your Apple gear.

A private external display that travels with your Mac

The GT Series also functions as an instant, private external display for a USB-C Mac. That makes the glasses invaluable far beyond streaming media, especially when you need an expansive, shoulder-surfer-proof dual-monitor workspace on a flight, train, or co-working desk.

Both GT and GT Max include three native 3DoF hardware display modes, meaning you can position your virtual screen around your head:

Follow keeps the display centered smoothly in front of you as you turn your head.

Pinned locks your virtual display in place in 3D space, letting you glance naturally between your MacBook keyboard and your floating multi-window setup.

Steady dampens micro-movements to keep the screen rock-solid on turbulent flights.

Because the tracking runs on dedicated silicon inside the glasses, none of it taxes the Mac or iPhone you’re plugged into. The glasses draw minimal power directly from the connected device and include a four-speaker spatial acoustic array co-tuned by Bang & Olufsen, with a directional Whisper Mode that cuts sound leakage on a plane or in an office. 

GT Max also comes in three sizes based on inter-pupillary distance (IPD) — small for under 64mm, medium for 64–67mm, large for over 67mm — ensuring a tailored, comfortable fit.

Keep speaking notes, live translations, and AI tools in view with RayNeo iO

If an everyday display frame came out of Cupertino today, it would look like RayNeo iO. Rather than heavy visors, iO pairs with your iPhone through the RayNeo app to project glanceable, contextual intelligence into genuine everyday eyewear.

iO uses a high-efficiency binocular MicroLED optical engine to float high-contrast green text into your sightline, presenting a virtual image equivalent to a 33-inch screen viewed from two meters away. With peak eye-level brightness rated at 1,300 nits, reading notes and prompts stays crystal clear even under direct midday sun without occluding your real-world surroundings. The waveguide is 97% transparent and the optical engine is hidden inside the frame, so from the outside these read as ordinary glasses — most people never clock them as smart eyewear at all.

For presentations and pitches, the built-in teleprompter scrolls your notes in sync with your natural speaking cadence, so you keep your eyes locked on your audience instead of looking down at your phone. During face-to-face meetings or international travel, the glasses deliver live subtitles and two-way translation right on the lenses, with support for 55 languages and 109 accents at roughly one second of latency.

Turn-by-turn navigation and an evolving suite of OTA features

Beyond live translation and teleprompting, RayNeo iO acts as a constantly evolving heads-up companion. RayNeo pushes frequent over-the-air (OTA) software updates, continually expanding what the glasses can do throughout your day.

Just now coming to iO is heads-up turn-by-turn navigation, which projects glanceable directional arrows, street names, and real-time transit alerts directly into your line of sight. Whether you’re walking through a new city or cycling down busy streets, you can navigate without holding your iPhone in front of you or looking down at your wrist. Alongside navigation, regular software updates continue to introduce new lifestyle tools, customizable notification filters, and contextual dashboard widgets that keep the hardware feeling fresh.

There’s more coming in December, too: RayNeo is opening the iO SDK to the public, so third-party apps — and community-built ones from people with no development background — start landing on the platform shortly after the holidays.

RayNeo iO’s productivity tools extend that concept further with a focus on personal privacy. This is where they really shine in the Apple ecosystem. A four-microphone array with a bone-conduction sensor captures clear audio for automated meeting minutes and AI summaries that extract key action items. RayNeo V1 and Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite are built in and free out of the box — no subscription required for everyday voice response, contextual reasoning, and ambient assistance. On the temple, an intuitive Smart Crown lets you scroll notifications and highlight key moments with familiar, physical micro-precision.

The titanium frames weigh just 33 grams and are rated IP54 for dust and water resistance, with a battery good for up to two days of typical use, 6.2 hours of continuous live translation, and a 25-minute charge to 80%.

iO supports Bluetooth 5.4 and carries Apple’s MFi (Made for iPhone) certification. It also has no speakers by design — which sounds like an omission until you realize what it buys you. RayNeo’s ultra-slim titanium temple arms sit flush against your ears and leave them completely free, so your AirPods stay in with Spatial Audio, Transparency Mode, and Active Noise Cancellation untouched for music and calls, while iO handles your heads-up visual intelligence.

title: Google Health 5.13 rolling out: Improved food search, more swimming controls
snippet: Version 5.13 of Google Health is rolling out to Android and iOS with updates across five areas. It’s a modest release that reiterates recent launches. more…
fullText:
Version 5.13 of Google Health is rolling out to Android and iOS with updates across five areas. It’s a modest release that reiterates recent launches.

Google is highlighting the availability of step-by-step workouts on the Pixel Watch 3, 4, and 5 as part of the November 2026 Pixel Drop. It rolled out with an update to the on-watch Google Health app, while we wait for Wear OS 7.1 to bring the other additions.

There’s also a reminder that apps and clocks are going away on older Fitbit OS smartwatches.

Activity and Fitness Updates

	

In-Progress Automatic Activity Detection: If you use your Pixel Watch, Fitbit Air, or Fitbit Edge to automatically track your exercises, you’ll now see an exercise-in-progress card on your mobile app’s Today screen. This card lets you know that your device is tracking your exercise and gives you the opportunity to end the tracking and get your summary whenever you want.

More Controls for Swimmers: You can now set your default pool length and unit preferences (meters or yards) for your swims for improved distance tracking. Go to your profile, then Google Health settings, and then Activity preferences to change your settings.

Step by Step Workouts: If you use Pixel Watch 3, 4, or 5, you can now get live step-by-step guidance on your watch during each exercise in your workout.  Learn more.

Nutrition Updates

Food search has been improved to help you more easily locate items.

More Options for Settings

You can now select ‘Prefer not to say’ or ‘An option not listed’ when selecting your sex during Google Health onboarding. If you select one of these options, you’ll then be asked to choose whether you’d like your metrics to be calculated based on studies of cisgender men or studies of cisgender women.

If your preferences change, you can find these settings at any time in the Health tab by scrolling to Personal info, tapping Profile, and editing your Sex settings.

Apple Health Sync Updates

We’ve fixed an issue that affected a small number of users after the daylight saving time change where Google Health stopped sending some data to Apple Health. Syncing will resume after this fix.  If you were impacted and still have gaps in your Apple Health data, sign out of the Google Health app and sign back in to send any missing data to Apple Health.

Apps and Clocks on Fitbit Smartwatches

Starting on November 28, 2026, you can no longer install or update third-party apps and clocks on Fitbit smartwatches.

After this date, your installed apps and clock faces from third-party developers will continue to work. However, if you choose to delete an app or clock face, or factory reset your device, you will no longer be able to re-install it.

You will continue to have access to a diverse gallery of apps and clocks developed by Fitbit and Google.

This change impacts users of Fitbit Sense, Fitbit Sense 2, Fitbit Versa 4, Fitbit Versa 3, Fitbit Versa 2, Fitbit Versa Lite, and Fitbit Versa.

iPadOS 27.3 is now in beta and will launch to all users next month, here are three new features it introduces for iPad.

#1: Double-tap top of window to resize

There’s a new setting in iPadOS 27.3 that I instantly turned on and have been loving. It lets you double-tap the top of a window to resize it.

Inside Settings ⇾ Multitasking & Gestures, if ‘Windowed Apps’ is enabled there’s now a new toggle: ‘Double-tap Top of Window to Zoom.’

I’ve been using this gesture all the time in the beta, because it lets me resize my window to fullscreen then revert it to its previous size with ease. It’s an intuitive, convenient way to resize windows for different tasks.

Read more: iPadOS 27.3 adds new iPad setting I instantly turned on

#2: Siri mode in Camera app

Visual intelligence was available on iPad already, but iPadOS 27.3 adds a dedicated hub for using the feature: a new Siri mode in the Camera app.

iOS 27 brought Siri mode to the iPhone’s Camera app, but it was missing from iPad. iPadOS 27.3 corrects that oversight, letting you use your iPad’s built-in Camera app to ask Siri about any object you capture.

Baking visual intelligence into Camera should expose the feature to a lot more iPad users, since before you had to set up a custom control or shortcut for it. And with how much better visual intelligence has gotten thanks to Siri AI, the Siri mode is a valuable addition.

title: iOS 27.3 beta can cause HomeView issues, Apple confirms
snippet: Apple’s new HomeView just launched last Friday, but some early adopters reported issues with Siri AI in their first days of use. Apple shipped fixes in HomeView 27.2.1 yesterday, but it also confirmed the iOS 27.3 beta is responsible for some of the problems. more…
fullText:
Apple’s new HomeView just launched last Friday, but some early adopters reported issues with Siri AI in their first days of use. Apple shipped fixes in HomeView 27.2.1 yesterday, but it also confirmed the iOS 27.3 beta is responsible for some of the problems.

HomeView 27.2.1 has Siri AI fixes, but iOS 27.3 beta users are now temporarily unable to perform Personal Content requests

Yesterday Apple released its first post-launch software update for HomeView, less than a week after the product debuted.

Per the company’s official release notes, HomeView 27.2.1 focuses on bug fixes, including a fix for the following issue:

Pairing with an iPhone or iPad running the iOS or iPadOS 27.3 beta may cause Siri requests to fail

It’s unknown how many reports of Siri issues on HomeView can be attributed to the iOS 27.3 beta. However, it wouldn’t surprise me if many of the reports were from beta users. That’s in part because early HomeView reviewers didn’t seem to have the same problems.

With HomeView 27.2.1 now available, those problems should hopefully be taken care of. However, if you’re on the iOS 27.3 beta, there’s a new issue you’ll need to deal with temporarily.

As discovered by pdfu, if you try to make a Personal Content request on an iPhone running iOS 27.3, Siri in HomeView 27.2.1 now says: “I can’t help with that because your personal device is on newer software.”

If you’re on iOS 27.3, Siri on HomeView can’t use your iPhone for personal context, likely until December.

HomeView won’t send Siri requests to an iPhone on newer software. Without a HomeView update, your only option is iOS 27.2.x.

On-device requests like timers still work. https://t.co/8UbRs7z496

— pdfu (@itspdfu) November 19, 2026

It’s understandable that issues might arise from having iOS and HomeView software that’s out of sync. Unfortunately though, there’s no beta software available for HomeView at the moment.

That means unless Apple releases a beta soon, users might have to wait until the public launch of HomeView 27.3 in December to get Personal Content features back.

title: Which Samsung folding phone is right for you? Galaxy Z Fold 8, Ultra, or Flip 8
snippet: Folding phones are entering a new chapter and, if you’re looking to try one for the first time, you might not know exactly where to start. In this guide, we’ll take a look at some of the most important questions to answer when buying a foldable, and dissect how Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, and Galaxy Z Flip 8 fit the bill to figure out which is the best for you, especially if you’re interested in one this holiday season. more…
fullText:
Folding phones are entering a new chapter and, if you’re looking to try one for the first time, you might not know exactly where to start. In this guide, we’ll take a look at some of the most important questions to answer when buying a foldable, and dissect how Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8, Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, and Galaxy Z Flip 8 fit the bill to figure out which is the best for you, especially if you’re interested in one this holiday season.

This post is sponsored by Samsung.

Galaxy Z Fold 8 vs Fold 8 Ultra vs Flip 8: What you need to know

Samsung has three foldables in its lineup this year, two of which are pretty familiar. The Galaxy Z Flip 8 continues the lineup of clamshell-style foldables, offering a form factor similar to that of a classic flip phone. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, meanwhile, is designed to be a normal smartphone on the outside, hiding a tablet within. Finally, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the new kid on the block, offering a compact outer display that opens up to a media-friendly, wider inner panel.

Each one serves a different need, but they all share similar performance and core specs. Here’s a quick rundown of the key details on each device:

	

Galaxy Z Fold 8

Displays: 5.5-inch outer, 7.6-inch inner, both up to 120Hz

Thickness: 9.7mm when folded

Weight: 201 grams

Chip: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy

Storage/RAM: Up to 1TB/16GB

Cameras: 50MP main, 50MP ultrawide, 10MP selfie (one on each display)

OS: One UI 9 based on Android 17

Battery: 4,800 mAh

Charging: 45W wired, 20W wireless

Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra

Displays: 6.5-inch outer, 8-inch inner, both up to 120Hz

Thickness: 8.9mm when folded

Weight: 215 grams

Chip: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy

Storage/RAM: Up to 1TB/16GB

Cameras: 200MP main, 50MP ultrawide, 10MP 3x telephoto, 10MP selfie (one on each display)

OS: One UI 9 based on Android 17

Battery: 5,000 mAh

Charging: 45W wired, 20W wireless

Galaxy Z Flip 8

Displays: 4.1-inch outer, 6.9-inch inner, both up to 120Hz

Thickness: 13.1mm when folded

Weight: 180 grams

Chip: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy

Storage/RAM: Up to 512GB/12GB

Cameras: 50MP main, 12MP ultrawide, 10MP selfie (on inner display)

OS: One UI 9 based on Android 17

Battery: 4,300 mAh

Charging: 25W wired, 15W wireless

Starting with the displays, the book-style Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Fold 8 Ultra both provide outer displays that are fully usable as standard smartphones, while the inner display is useful for multitasking, media, or just getting more space for reading a website or e-book. Samsung’s top-tier specs deliver performance for everything you’d need, with Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy powering everything from demanding games or media-editing apps to day-to-day use.

With each Samsung foldable, you’re getting a fully capable smartphone, but finding the one that’s best for you is a matter of picking your most important priorities. Cameras, battery life, content consumption, and size are some of the most important points to consider, so let’s take a look one-by-one.

What Samsung foldable has the best cameras?

When it comes to cameras, foldables have a tough time. There’s only so much physical space to fit the camera sensors and, with cameras, having more space generally results in a battery overall camera.

That said, the best camera on a Samsung foldable is undoubtedly on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. 

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a 200MP main camera that’s similar to the Galaxy S26 Ultra, while it also packs a 50MP ultrawide and something neither of the others offer, a telephoto lens. The 10MP telephoto shooter captures faraway subjects at 3x optical zoom, meaning you’re not giving up on quality when you zoom in. Two 10MP cameras can be found on the displays, with neither sacrificing quality for an under-display look.

Runner-up here is the Galaxy Z Fold 8, which offers a pair of 50MP cameras for wide and ultrawide shots. You can get 2x optical-quality zoom out of the main sensor to still get a good zoom shot, while the main camera still offers good quality and Samsung’s best camera features including 2x optical-quality zoom and the subject-tracking My FanCam.

The Galaxy Z Flip 8 may not have the best camera hardware, but what it lacks in hardware it makes up for in flexibility. This is definitely the best form factor of the bunch for using the foldable design as a tripod for capturing clips. All three devices also use their foldable nature to let you capture full-quality selfies using the rear cameras, which always have better quality than the 10MP dedicated front-facing cameras. 

What Samsung foldable has the best battery life?

Here’s where specs on paper can tell a different story compared to real life. 

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra may offer the biggest battery of the bunch at 5,000 mAh, but its battery life is on par with the smaller Galaxy Z Fold 8. Both foldables are designed to last you through a full day, though sticking to the outer display only on the Fold 8 Ultra may bring you slightly better battery life overall.

In either case, you’re also getting 45W fast charging over USB-C, granting you speedy recharging if your device happens to get low through the course of a busy day. These are also “Qi2 Ready,” meaning you can use magnetic wireless chargers if you use a compatible magnetic case.

Why buy a folding phone in the first place?

One of the most important things you’ll want to ask yourself when buying a foldable phone is why you want to opt for a foldable in the first place, and each of these devices gives a different answer.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is a productivity powerhouse, delivering more space on its inner display for you to get work done through the web, apps, and more. You can run up to three apps at once on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra’s display, as well as floating apps, and more. 

Galaxy Z Fold 8 is great for media consumption. The wider aspect ratio is perfect for watching videos, playing games, reading books, and more, all while still giving you plenty of space for productivity just like the Ultra. 

Galaxy Z Flip 8, meanwhile, is all about giving you a more compact device. The outer display lets you quickly reply to messages or keep up with directions, while you can unfold it to do everything you want to on a normal phone. Close it up to more easily stow it away in your pocket or your bag.

Can I transfer everything from my old phone?

If you are moving into a new Galaxy foldable, the good news is that you don’t have to start from scratch. Thanks to Samsung’s Smart Switch app, you can easily transfer supported content including pictures, contacts, messages, and more from an older Galaxy phone, another Android phone, or even an iPhone over to a Galaxy foldable. Apps, messages, photos, and more can all make the move wirelessly, without the need of a cable.

Where to buy a Samsung foldable

You can get the Galaxy Z Fold 8, Fold 8 Ultra, and Flip 8 from your favorite carriers and retailers, but Best Buy is one of the best places to score a great deal with solid trade-in values and deep discounts around Black Friday and throughout the holiday season.

title: Siri Modular Apple Watch face gains two new styles with watchOS 27.3
snippet: Siri Modular, the new Apple Watch face in watchOS 27, is gaining new style options. watchOS 27.3, currently in beta, adds two more style options to the existing set. This gives users five options for adjusting what type of information appears on Siri Modular. more…
fullText:
Siri Modular, the new Apple Watch face in watchOS 27, is gaining new style options. watchOS 27.3, currently in beta, adds two more style options to the existing set. This gives users five options for adjusting what type of information appears on Siri Modular. 

watchOS 27.3 adds two Siri-focused styles to Siri Modular

Siri Modular originally shipped with three style options. Each supports a small line complication above the time. 

Additionally, the original three styles include these options:

Large digital click + three circular complications

Compact digital clock + Smart Stack tile + three circular complications 

Large digital clock + Smart Stack tile

In watchOS 27.3, Apple introduces two new Siri features that work with Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4.

First, there’s Siri Recap which uses the Apple Watch to turn audio into high-level text summaries. Second, there’s Live Rewind which lets you view a transcript of the last 15 seconds of spoken word.

The two new Siri Modular Apple Watch face styles help surface three things: invoking Siri, viewing conversations with Siri, and viewing Siri Recaps on the Apple Watch.

The new styles include a pill-shaped module that includes icon shortcuts that go directly to Siri conversations, invoke Siri AI, or go directly to Siri Recaps in the Siri app.

One style features a large digital clock with the new three-button Siri module. Another includes a compact digital clock with a Smart Stack tile and the new three-button Siri module.

This brings the style options to five. If you use the three circular complications configuration, you can also assign a Siri icon that invokes Siri AI. 

watchOS 27.3 is currently in beta and expected to be released officially in December.

title: Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 vs Watch 9: When is it right to spend more?
snippet: The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is worth spending more on if you want longer battery life, a brighter outdoor display, and specialized features for trail running and diving. The Galaxy Watch 9 is the better fit if you want Samsung’s latest everyday health tools in a smaller, lighter watch. Both, however, are fantastic smartwatches with limitless potential. They share a Snapdragon Wear Elite processor and many of Samsung’s newest wellness features, so deciding between them is really about figuring out your priorities when it comes to buying a wearable this holiday season. We’re here to help you figure that out. more…
fullText:
The Samsung Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is worth spending more on if you want longer battery life, a brighter outdoor display, and specialized features for trail running and diving. The Galaxy Watch 9 is the better fit if you want Samsung’s latest everyday health tools in a smaller, lighter watch.

Both, however, are fantastic smartwatches with limitless potential. They share a Snapdragon Wear Elite processor and many of Samsung’s newest wellness features, so deciding between them is really about figuring out your priorities when it comes to buying a wearable this holiday season. We’re here to help you figure that out.

This post is sponsored by Samsung.

What do the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 and Watch 9 have in common?

As we covered in our Galaxy Watch 9 and Watch Ultra 2 comparison, both watches move to Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Wear Elite platform. Both also ship with Wear OS 7 and One UI 8 Watch.

	

That shared foundation includes useful health insights. Vitals brings overnight measurements together to establish your personal baseline, while Daily Cardio Load helps you understand training demands and recovery. Hearing monitoring can flag potentially unsafe noise levels, whether you’re at a concert or somewhere unexpectedly loud.

Both also get five years of Wear OS updates and security patches, making either a useful long-term partner for your Samsung device, like the Galaxy S26 Ultra or Galaxy Z Fold8.

How do their specifications compare?

The clearest differences are size, battery capacity, display brightness, and outdoor capabilities. Here’s how the lineup breaks down:
